functions.name: leReturnToLevel
functions.description: Applies to instances, nested instances, groups, and nested groups for which you are editing-in-place. For instances, returns one or more levels up the hierarchy from the current level in the instance you last edited-in-place. When there is only one level, exits Edit-in-Place mode. When you have descended more than one level, this function displays the Return To Level form, showing the levels to which you can return. You select (highlight) the desired level and click OK. For example, if you are using leHiEditInPlace to edit a cellview two levels deep in your hierarchy, you can use leReturnToLevel to move up one or two levels in the hierarchy. For groups, returns from the group, and if the group is nested, from all groups in the nesting, and exits Edit-in-Place mode. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

functions.name: leReturnToTop
functions.description: Applies to instances, nested instances, groups, and nested groups for which you are editing-in-place. When editing instances or nested instances in Edit-in-Place mode, returns to top level, exits Edit-in-Place mode. For groups, returns from the group, and if the group is nested, from all groups in the nesting, and exits Edit-in-Place mode. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

functions.name: leSaveMarkNet
functions.signature: leSaveMarkNet(cellName[ ?libName t_libName ][ ?viewName t_viewName ][ ?pt l_pt ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Saves a particular highlighted net at the specified point (l_point). If no point is specified, all the highlighted nets in current cellview are saved in the specified cellview (lib/cell/view).

functions.name: leSearchHierarchy
functions.description: Searches the cellview d_cellViewId for objects that match the type and criteria specified. The search is bound by the specified l_bBox and restricted to the specified x_stopLevel. The search assumes all figures are valid if the Layer Selection Window (LSW) has not been initialized.

functions.name: leSelBoxOrStretch
functions.description: The Virtuoso Layout Suite L binds this function to the mouse button DrawThru1 action. The default behavior for mouse button DrawThru1 is select by bBox. When you select using a bBox, rather than a point, the software checks what is under the selected area. If something under the initial point of the bBox is already selected, the software automatically calls the stretch command. If nothing under the cursor is selected, the software selects the bBox you have drawn. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used. This function must not be changed.

functions.name: leSetAllGridObjectsVisible
functions.description: Sets all LSW grid pane objects to visible if g_isVisible is t, or invisible if g_isVisible is nil.

functions.name: leSetAllLayerSelectable
functions.description: Sets the selectability of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetAllLayerValid
functions.description: Sets the validity of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isValid. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetAllLayerVisible
functions.description: Sets the visibility of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetAllObjectsSelectable
functions.description: Sets the selectability of LSW objects in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not given, the current LSW technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetAllObjectsVisible
functions.description: Sets the visibility of LSW objects in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not given, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetAreaEstimatorParameters
functions.description: Opens a form to update the parameter list to new values. On pressing OK on the form, the updated parameter list is returned.

functions.name: leSetEditFigGroup
functions.description: Sets the Edit-In-Place context for editing a specific group within a nested set of groups. For example, when fgBottom is contained in fgMiddle, and fgMiddle, is contained in fgTop, you can use this function and the figGroup ID for fgBottom to start Edit-in-Place for fgBottom.

functions.name: leSetEntryLayer
functions.description: Sets the entry layer for technology file d_techFileId to the layer specified by l_layerPurposePair, which can be either a list containing a layer name and a layer purpose, or just a layer name (the layer purpose then defaults to drawing). If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetEnv
functions.description: Sets the layout environment properties with the variable t_name to the value g_value.

functions.name: leSetFocusToEditableFieldsInStatusToolbar
functions.description: Sets the focus to the editable X field on the Status toolbar of the window, w_windowId.

functions.name: leSetFormSnapMode
functions.description: Sets the cursor snap mode in a valid active window.

functions.name: leSetGlobalGridsVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility of global snap pattern grids.

functions.name: leSetInstSelectable
functions.description: Sets the selectability of instances in the technology file specified by d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetLSWFilter
functions.description: Specifies which layer-purpose pairs in the technology database to display in the Layer Selection Window (LSW). You can include one or more of the following types of layers: valid layers, rule layers, user layers.

functions.name: leSetLayerAttributes
functions.description: Sets the attributes of the specified layer in the technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_layerPurposePair and l_attributeList.

functions.name: leSetLayerSelectable
functions.description: Sets the selectability of shapes on layer l_layerPurposePair in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used. For shapes on a layer to be selectable, the layer must be valid, visible, and selectable.

functions.name: leSetLayerValid
functions.description: Sets the validity of layer l_layerPurposePair as specified by g_isValid. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used. Only valid layers are displayed in the Layer Selection Window.

functions.name: leSetLayerVisible
functions.description: Sets the visibility of the layer specified by the layer-purpose pair as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file Layer Selection Window (LSW) is used.

functions.name: leSetLocalGridsVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility of local snap pattern grids.

functions.name: leSetObjectSelectable
functions.description: Turns on or off the selectability of the layers used for objectName or updates the selectability of instances or pins as specified by g_isSelectable.

functions.name: leSetObjectVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility of the layers used for objectName or updates the visibility of instances or pins as specified by g_isVisible.

functions.name: leSetPinSelectable
functions.description: Sets the selectability of pins in the technology file specified by d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

functions.name: leSetRefPoint
functions.description: Sets the reference point of cellview d_cellViewId to the point l_point. The reference point is set to be active if it was inactive.

functions.name: leSetRefPointInactive
functions.description: Marks the reference point for cellview d_cellViewId as inactive. To make a reference point active again, use leSetRefPoint.

functions.name: leSetSnapPatternVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility of the specified snap pattern grid.

functions.name: leSetStopLevelToEditLevel
functions.description: Sets the display stop level to the current editing level.

functions.name: leSetStopLevelToMaxHierDepth
functions.description: Sets the display stop level to the maximum hierarchy depth, which is 31.

functions.name: leSetWidthSpacingSnapPatternVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility of the specified width spacing snap pattern grid.

functions.name: leSetWirebondProfileVisible
functions.description: (Virtuoso RF Option) Sets the visibility of the specified wirebond profile.

functions.name: leSizeShape
functions.description: Resizes a shape by the specified amount. A shape can be resized uniformly in all directions or differently in different directions.

functions.name: leSlice
functions.description: Performs the vertical slicing of a shape.

functions.name: leSpaceBarFunc
functions.signature: leSpaceBarFunc([ w_windowId ][ g_useDefault ][ g_shift ])=> return value from the called function
functions.description: Invokes the function specified by name in the Virtuoso Layout Suite L environment variable spaceFuncName when the g_useDefault argument is set to t. When the g_useDefault argument is set to nil the space bar is not used as a bindkey. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

functions.name: leSplitShape
functions.description: Splits a shape and moves one portion of it. Uses a multi-segment split line to divide the shape.

functions.name: leStartRouter
functions.signature: leStartRouter([ ?layoutLCV list(t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName) ][ ?layoutRoutedLCV list(t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName) ][ ?constraintGroup t_constraintGroupName ][ ?doFile S_doFile ][ ?initCommand S_initCommand ][ ?showGraphics g_showGraphics ][ ?quitAtFinish g_quitAtFinish ][ ?useStartupFiles g_useStartupFiles ][ ?usePreroutes g_usePreroutes ][ ?usePreroutedIO g_usePreroutedIO ][ ?stripOrphanShapes g_stripOrphanShapes ][ ?checkAtStartup g_checkAtStartup ][ ?cutKeepoutByClearance g_cutKeepoutByClearance ][ ?cutKeepoutToImageEdge g_cutKeepoutToImageEdge ][ ?createDidFile g_createDidFile ][ ?didFile S_didFile ][ ?messageFile S_messageFile ][ ?statusFile S_statusFile ][ ?startupOptions S_startupOptions ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Starts the Virtuoso Chip Assembly Router with specified data and startup options.

functions.name: leStretchFig
functions.description: Stretches shape d_shapeId by the delta l_delta. Donuts cannot be stretched.

functions.name: leStretchShape
functions.description: Stretches shape d_shapeId by the delta l_delta. Donuts cannot be stretched.

functions.name: leToggleAllGravity
functions.description: Toggles the gravity and rule gravity settings. If the values of gravity (cdsenv gravityOn) and rule gravity (cdsenv ruleGravityOn) are different, leToggleAllGravity() turns on the value of both the environment variables to make them equal.

functions.name: leToggleAutoZoomPan
functions.description: Toggles the current value of dynamic zoom for the specified w_windowId. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

functions.name: leToggleDrdMode
functions.description: Cycles through DRD modes: Off, Notify, Enforce, and Enforce and Notify.

functions.name: leToggleGravity
functions.description: Turns gravity on or off.

functions.name: leToggleKeepFirstName
functions.description: Toggles the Keep First Name option on or off on the Create Pin form. When this option is on, you can create multiple pins with the same terminal name.

functions.name: leToggleMagnifier
functions.description: Toggles the visibility of the magnifier between on and off.

functions.name: leToggleMaintainConnections
functions.description: Turns Maintain Connections on or off.

functions.name: leToggleRuleGravity
functions.description: Turns rule gravity on or off.

functions.name: leToggleSmartSnap
functions.description: Toggles the smart snap mode of ruler between no snapping (off) and snap to any target (on).

functions.name: leUnRegAreaEstimator
functions.description: Unregisters a particular area estimation function for one or more object types.

functions.name: leUnRegClusterBdyEstimator
functions.description: Unregisters the name of the estimator which will subsequently no longer appear in the cyclic field of the Area Estimator field in the Create Cluster Boundary form in Layout XL.

functions.name: leUnfreezeInst
functions.description: Unfreezes or converts the non-Pcell instance, d_instId, to its original Pcell instance. When an instance is unfreezed the leUnfreezeInst() function only re-evaluates the Pcell instance but does not explicitly call the CDF callbacks.

functions.name: leUniquifyCellView
functions.description: Opens the Uniquify form to specify the library, cell, and view name of the cellview to be uniquified. Alternatively, you can use the Uniquify command on the Tools menu in the CIW. A message displays after the successful uniquification of the cellview. If the cellview is already uniquified or the cellview cannot be opened, the command exits and displays an appropriate message.

functions.name: leUnmarkNet
functions.description: Deletes the highlighting of the marked nets in the current cellview. This function can delete the highlights of a particular net at the specified point (l_point). If no point is specified, the highlights of all the marked nets in current cellview are deleted.

functions.name: leUnregUserLayerSelectionFilter
functions.description: Unregisters user defined layer selection filter.

functions.name: leUnregUserObjectSelectionFilter
functions.description: Unregisters user defined object selection filter.

functions.name: leUnregisterUseGravity
functions.description: Prevents a user-defined SKILL enter function to use gravity. By default, gravity is available only for SKILL enter functions for which gravity has been enabled using the leRegisterUseGravity function.

functions.name: leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues
functions.description: Updates the list of CDF parameters name-value pairs for the specified cellview and instance.

functions.name: leWECycleControlWire
functions.description: Allows cycling through the extreme and middle control wires in the selected bus during interactive bus editing. This functions runs successfully only when the Create Wire command is active. This function is available only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

functions.name: leWECycleSnap
functions.description: Allows cycling of highlight during the Create Wire command through level 1 or top-level pin edges available within the Aperture distance from the cursor. The highlighted edge represents the starting point of wire creation.

functions.name: leWENoSnap
functions.description: Resets the point of starting wire creation to the current location of the cursor during the Create Wire command.

functions.name: leYankFigs
functions.description: Copies specified objects into a yank buffer for later pasting. Copies objects in cellview d_cellViewId that fall within the shape defined by the points in l_ptArray and that are in the levels of hierarchy specified by x_nLevels. Optionally uses l_refPt as the reference point for the yank and x_nSides as the number of polygon sides to use when converting objects intersected by the yank shape.

functions.name: leZoomToPoint
functions.description: Places the cursor in the window, w_windowId, at the coordinates specified in l_points.

functions.name: leZoomToSelSet
functions.description: Zooms to fit the selected objects in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

functions.name: leafValue
functions.description: Returns the leaf waveform or the leaf value from the specified family of waveforms.

functions.name: leftEdge
functions.description: Returns the lower left point's X coordinate of the figure's bounding box.

functions.name: leftshift
functions.description: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the left. Prefix form of the << arithmetic operator. leftshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

functions.name: leiDiscardEdits
functions.description: Discards all edits you made since the last time you saved. Corresponds to the cellview window Design - Discard Edits command.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Determines the length of a list, array, association table, or string.

functions.name: leqp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the <= operator.

functions.name: lessp
functions.description: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than the second argument. Prefix form of the < operator.

functions.name: let
functions.signature: SKILL modelet(l_bindingsg_expr1 ...)=> g_resultSKILL++ modelet([ s_var ](( s_var1 s_initExp1 )( s_var2 s_initExp2 )...)body)=> g_result
functions.description: In the SKILL mode, this function provides a faster alternative to prog for binding local variables only. This is a syntax form. In the SKILL++ mode, this function declares a lexical scope. This includes a collection of local variables, as well as body expressions to be evaluated. This becomes a named let if the optional s_var is given.

functions.name: letrec
functions.signature: letrec((( s_var1 s_initExp1 )( s_var2 s_initExp2 )...)body)=> g_result
functions.description: (SKILL++ mode) A letrec expression can be used in SKILL++ mode only. All the bindings are in effect while their initial values are being computed, thus allowing mutually recursive definitions. Use letrec to declare recursive local functions.

functions.name: letseq
functions.signature: letseq((( s_var1 initExp1 )( s_var2 initExp2 )...)body)=> g_result
functions.description: A letseq expression can be used in both SKILL and SKILL++ modes. The bindings and evaluations are performed sequentially.

functions.name: linRg
functions.description: Returns a list of numbers in the linear range from n_from to n_to incremented by n_by.

functions.name: lindex
functions.description: Returns the index number of the given element in l_list.

functions.name: lineread
functions.description: Parses the next line in the input port into a list that you can further manipulate. It is used by the interpreter's top level to read in all input and understands SKILL and SKILL++ syntax.

functions.name: linereadstring
functions.description: Executes lineread on a string and returns the first form read in. Anything after the first form is ignored.

functions.name: list
functions.description: Creates a list with the given elements.

functions.name: listAlias
functions.description: Prints a (property) list of all current aliases and associated function symbols, or the function symbol for which the given alias is defined.

functions.name: listFunctions
functions.description: Returns all public function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression. If the second (optional) argument is specified as t (or a non-nil value), listFunctions looks at the SKILL virtual machine, rather than the cdsFinder database, and returns all isCallable Cadence public functions and user-defined SKILL functions that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

functions.name: listToVector
functions.description: Returns a vector (array) filled with the elements from the given list. A vector is represented by an array.

functions.name: listVariables
functions.description: Returns all variable names that match the given substring or regular expression as part or all of their print name.

functions.name: listp
functions.description: Checks whether the specified object is a list.

functions.name: lmCheckTerm
functions.description: Checks the consistency of terminal name, type, and wth for all views of each specified cell.

functions.name: lmCheckView
functions.description: Evaluates a sequence of expressions for each specified cellview. Checks the property value for consistency.

functions.name: lmCloseLib
functions.description: Closes the previously opened working library.

functions.name: lmDefTermProp
functions.signature: lmDefTermProp([ t_cellName ][ t_viewName ]( g_terminalList t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName = t_propertyValue )( g_terminalList t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue ))
functions.description: Adds properties to the terminals of the specified cellview. To add terminal properties, add specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

functions.name: lmDefViewProp
functions.signature: lmDefViewProp([ t_cellName ][ t_viewName ]( t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue ))
functions.description: Adds properties to the specified cellview. To add properties, add the specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

functions.name: lmDeleteTermProp
functions.description: Deletes specified properties from the terminals of specified views.

functions.name: lmDeleteViewProp
functions.description: Deletes specified properties from the specified view.

functions.name: lmGetValue
functions.description: Returns the value of a specified view property in the current referenced view.

functions.name: lmLoadData
functions.signature: lmLoadData(t_filet_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Opens a working library, loads the library command file, and closes the library when you are finished.

functions.name: lmOpenLib
functions.signature: lmOpenLib(t_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Opens a library.

functions.name: lmPrintLibTermProp
functions.description: Prints terminal properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

functions.name: lmPrintLibViewProp
functions.description: Prints properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

functions.name: lmPrintTerm
functions.description: Prints names, types, and wths of all terminals of the specified cellviews.

functions.name: lmPrintTermProp
functions.description: Prints properties of all terminals of the specified views of a cell.

functions.name: lmPrintViewProp
functions.description: Prints properties of all specified views of a cell.

functions.name: lmReset
functions.description: Resets all global variables to their default values.

functions.name: lmSimView
functions.description: Creates a view with specified properties for the specified cell.

functions.name: lmgrAddMenuItems
functions.description: Appends the named objects to the specified menu. An item can be another menu. Each menu item or menu can be added to only one menu. Likewise, any menu item can appear at most once in every pop-up menu. Menus cannot be added to a pop-up. Pop-ups must remain a flat structure only. Pop-ups cannot be added to menus.

functions.name: lmgrAddToolBarItems
functions.description: Adds menu items with the specified names to the Library Manager toolbar and optionally appends additional items with multiple calls. Item icons can be set using lmgrSetObject.

functions.name: lmgrCreateMenu
functions.description: Creates a structure for a menu, which can be populated with menu items. Once this menu is created, you can install it into the top menu bar or into another parent menu using lmgrAddMenuItems.

functions.name: lmgrCreateMenuItem
functions.description: Creates an instance of a menu item, which should be populated into a single menu. Once this menu item is created, you can install it into a menu using lmgrAddMenuItems().

functions.name: lmgrDefineInits
functions.description: Defines the initialization action to perform when the customization code begins (after parsing the extension file) and the termination action to perform immediately before Library Manager terminates. You must define the callback in the Virtuoso program before it starts. Otherwise, you get an error. No arguments are passed to either callback.

functions.name: lmgrDeleteMenuItems
functions.description: Deletes the named objects from the menu/pop-up hierarchy. The object can be either a single item or an entire menu. There is no recovery or undo from this operation. If you merely wish to temporarily disable the view of an object, consider using lmgrManageMenuItems() instead.

functions.name: lmgrDisplayMessage
functions.description: Displays a string in the Message area on the Library Manager form and appends it to the Library Manager log file. If desired, the message can be written just to the Library Manager log file and not echoed to the user. Ensure that the string is terminated by a newline character, or the string might be confused with the output from other Library Manager commands or other calls to this function.

functions.name: lmgrGetObject
functions.description: Returns a list describing the state of the single named object or nil if the object does not exist. The format of the attribute list will be variable length list of tags (strings) paired with matching values that are either a string or Boolean value.

functions.name: lmgrInsertMenuItems
functions.description: Inserts the named objects into the menu directly before the indicated menu item. An object can be an entire menu. Each menu item or menu can be inserted or added to only one menu. Likewise, any menu item can appear at most once in each pop-up menu. Menus can not be inserted (added) to a pop-up. Pop-ups must remain a flat structure only. You cannot insert or add pop-ups to menus. This function is similar to lmgrAddMenuItems(), except in the meaning of the first argument.

functions.name: lmgrLogShowPopup
functions.description: Restores the context for popup menus for Library Manager replay. This function is only intended for supporting replay and cannot be called from other SKILL engine programs. You do not need to use this function directly.

functions.name: lmgrManageMenuItems
functions.description: Manages the named objects (enabling the display of named objects) inside their menu hierarchy and pop-up sets. Objects can be either a single item or an entire menu.

functions.name: lmgrMenuSubsInPopup
functions.description: This API is used only in the Library Manager's cdsLibMgr.il file for menu customization. The named menu may be placed into a sub-menu of a popup menu, which appears on clicking the right mouse button (RMB) in the Library Manager's window that lists the library, cell, and view items being browsed. This will be placed in a sub-popup if the boolean value was set to be true. In addition, menu items tagged for adding to the popup menus are displayed within its menu's sub-popup (if any). Sub-popup menus may be hierarchically nested per menu as they have been setup/defined through the customized menus' hierarchy.

functions.name: lmgrQueryNamedObjects
functions.description: Returns a list containing the names of all menu items in the Library Manager menu named t_menuName.

functions.name: lmgrRemoveToolBarItems
functions.description: Removes the specified items from the given toolbar that were previously added using lmgrAddToolBarItems.

functions.name: lmgrSensitizeMenuItems
functions.description: Sensitizes the named objects (enabling the active state of named objects) inside their menu hierarchy and pop-up sets. Objects can be either a single item or an entire menu.

functions.name: lmgrSetObject
functions.description: Accepts a list describing the state of the named object. Returns nil if the object does not exist. The format of the attribute list is a variable-length list of tags (strings) paired with matching string or Boolean values.

functions.name: lmgrShowToolBar
functions.description: Displays the specified toolbar when the Library Manager is launched and returns the previous show state specified.

functions.name: lmgrValidateIcon
functions.description: Checks whether an icon file exists in the Library Manager for the specified icon name before creating a menu item.

functions.name: lmgrVerbose
functions.description: Aids in debugging the callbacks registered in the cdsLibMgr.il file. It is possible to get additional informational messages to be shown inshown in the CIW.

functions.name: ln
functions.signature: ln({ o_waveform | n_number })=> o_waveform / f_number / nil
functions.description: Gets the base-e (natural) logarithm of a waveform or number.

functions.name: lntAddTrace
functions.signature: lntAddTrace(w_window{ d_figId | t_netName }[ ?mode t_mode ][ ?hierPath l_hierPath ][ ?startLevel x_startLevel ][ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ][ ?userArea l_userArea ][ ?hilightIncrementally g_hilightIncrementally ][ ?retainColornStateInfo g_retainColornStateInfo ][ ?hilightColor t_hilightColor ][ ?maxCutShapes t_maxCutShapes ][ ?constraintGroup t_constraintGroup ][ ?stackLayers l_stackLayers ])=> x_traceId / nil
functions.description: Creates a trace starting from the specified figure or net name in the specified window.

functions.name: lntClearNeighbors
functions.description: Deletes all computed neighbors in the specified window.

functions.name: lntComputeNeighbors
functions.description: Finds neighboring shapes for the existing traces in the specified window, within the given distance, on the same layer or any extractable layer and creates highlights for the overlapped portions.

functions.name: lntContSteps
functions.description: Generates the complete trace from the current step to the last when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntGetAllTraces
functions.description: Lists all the traces in the specified cellview.

functions.name: lntGetCurrentStep
functions.description: Returns the current step value when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntGetSavedViewNames
functions.description: Returns the list of views saved in the specified library and cell.

functions.name: lntGetTailVal
functions.description: Returns the current value of the tail of a trace when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntGetTraceInfo
functions.description: Returns information for a specified trace. The returned information contains the trace container, its name, color, and visibility status, and the number of chased shapes.

functions.name: lntHiEditTrace
functions.description: Invokes the Net Tracer Edit In Place command that lets you edit in place the instances that contain the traced objects.

functions.name: lntHiNetTracer
functions.description: Invokes the Net Tracer command, which you can use to add, update, or delete traces in a layout window.

functions.name: lntHideNeighbors
functions.description: Hides displayed neighbors for the specified window. The computed neighbors are retained and can be displayed again using the lntShowNeighbors command. Use lntClearNeighbors to delete all neighbors.

functions.name: lntIsNeighborsVisible
functions.description: Checks whether Net Tracer neighbors are visible in the specified window.

functions.name: lntIsStepTrace
functions.description: Checks whether the specified trace was created using Step mode.

functions.name: lntNeighbors
functions.description: Displays the Net Tracer Neighbors form, which you can use to compute all neighboring shapes within a given distance for all the traces in the window.

functions.name: lntNextStep
functions.description: Increments the current step value by one when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntNextToSetStep
functions.description: Forwards tracing of all Step mode traces to the newly specified step value. For information about how the SKILL function behaves differently for each trace, depending on the maximum step value for the trace, see Additional Information.

functions.name: lntPrevStep
functions.description: Decrements the current step value by one when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntRemoveAll
functions.description: Removes all traces created by the Net Tracer command from the current layout window.

functions.name: lntRemoveAllTraces
functions.description: Removes all traces from the specified window.

functions.name: lntRemoveTrace
functions.description: Removes the specified trace from the specified window.

functions.name: lntSaveTraces
functions.signature: lntSaveTraces(w_windowIDl_traceIDlibNamecellNameviewName[ g_saveNeighbors ][ g_appendTraces ][ g_replaceSameNameTrace ][ ?oneViewPerTrace g_oneViewPerTrace ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Saves the shapes of the specified traces that are displayed in the library cellview open in the specified window.

functions.name: lntSetCurrentStep
functions.description: Sets the current step value for a trace when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntSetTailVal
functions.description: Sets the current value of the tail for all traces when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

functions.name: lntSetTraceColor
functions.description: Changes the color of the specified trace to the specified color in the given window.

functions.name: lntSetTraceVisibility
functions.description: Sets the visibility of the specified trace in the specified window.

functions.name: lntShowHideAllTraces
functions.description: Shows or hides all traces in the cellview contained in the specified window.

functions.name: lntShowNeighbors
functions.description: Displays computed neighbors for the specified window. The computed neighbors can be hidden using the lntHideNeighbors SKILL function. Use lntClearNeighbors to delete all neighbors.

functions.name: load
functions.description: Opens a file and repeatedly calls lineread to read in the file, immediately evaluating each form after it is read in.

functions.name: loadContext
functions.description: Loads a context file into the current session.

functions.name: loadPort
functions.description: Loads a SKILL file from p_port.

functions.name: loadStability
functions.description: Computes the load stability circles.

functions.name: loadTopContextForms
functions.signature: loadTopContextForms(t_FileName[ ?debugMode g_debugMode ][ ?writeProtect g_writeProtect ][ ?writeProtectAll g_writeProtectAll ][ ?lazyComp g_lazyComp ][ ?printinfix g_printinfix ][ ?integermode g_integermode ][ ?mergemode g_mergemode ][ ?readProtect g_readProtect ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Loads top-level SKILL or Scheme forms from a file. If the setContext mode is set, these forms are saved in a context. After the context is loaded, these forms are evaluated at the top-level, as if these were loaded from an .il or .ils file.

functions.name: loadi
functions.description: Identical to load, except that loadi ignores errors encountered during the load, prints an error message, and then continues loading.

functions.name: loadpull
functions.description: Plots load pull contour for the given waveform of PSS analysis. This function works only for two-dimensional sweep PSS results. The inner sweep should be phase and the outer sweep should be magnitude.

functions.name: loadstring
functions.description: Opens a string for reading, then parses and executes expressions stored in the string, just as load does in loading a file.

functions.name: lobAddCopyFill
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Identifies gaps in the row regions in the given target area and fills them with the specified target fill cells.

functions.name: lobBaseLayerDummyFillCB
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Invokes the Fill tab of the Auto P&R assistant.

functions.name: lobBaseLayerDummyFillWrapperCB
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Checks for license availability before invoking the Fill tab of the Auto P&R assistant.

functions.name: lobGetRegUserProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Returns a list of strings that contain the name of the specified registered user procedure.

functions.name: lobGetRegisteredAdjacentFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Returns the name of the function that is registered as the adjacent fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobGetRegisteredFillOverrideParameters
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Returns the first set of registered fill override parameters that matches the specified library and cell names.

functions.name: lobGetRegisteredTransitionFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Returns the name of the function that is registered as the transition fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobIsCopyFill
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Checks whether the specified object has been created using the copy fill functions.

functions.name: lobRegUserProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Registers a user-defined function for a specific purpose, as needed by layout objects. This function is currently used to register procedures to retrieve adjacent fill definitions.

functions.name: lobRegisterAdjacentFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Registers the specified user function symbol as the adjacent fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobRegisterFillOverrideParameters
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Registers parameter overrides to be used by dummy fill. Lookup processes parameter overrides in the order in which they are registered.

functions.name: lobRegisterTransitionFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Registers the specified user function symbol as the transition fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobRemoveCopyFill
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Removes all objects copy that were created using the copy fill functions from the specified cellview.

functions.name: lobUnRegUserProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Accepts user functions based on keyword and unregisters them.

functions.name: lobUnRegisterAdjacentFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Unregisters the specified user function symbol, which is currently registered as the adjacent fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobUnRegisterTransitionFillDefsProc
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Unregisters the specified user function symbol that is currently registered as the transition fill definition procedure.

functions.name: lobUnregisterFillOverrideParameters
functions.description: (Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL) Unregisters either all registered fill parameter overrides for the given library name or all the currently registered fill parameters for all libraries.

functions.name: log
functions.description: Returns the natural logarithm of a floating-point number or integer.

functions.name: log10
functions.signature: log10({ o_waveform | n_number })=> o_waveform / n_number / nil
functions.description: Gets the base-10 logarithm of a waveform or a number.

functions.name: logRg
functions.description: Returns a list of numbers in the log10 range from n_from to n_to advanced by n_by.

functions.name: lowerCase
functions.description: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with uppercase alphabetic characters replaced by their lowercase equivalents.

functions.name: lowerLeft
functions.description: Returns the lower left point of the given bounding box. The bounding box is not validated and assumed to be correct.

functions.name: lsb
functions.description: Computes the load stability circles.

functions.name: lshift
functions.description: Shifts the waveform to the left by the delta value.

functions.name: lsprintf
functions.description: Returns a string according to the provided format. lsprintf is a lambda version of the sprintf function that can be used as an argument with apply or funcall.

functions.name: lxAbutGetNeighbors
functions.signature: lxAbutGetNeighbors({ ld_instId | d_instId }[ ?direction { 'up | 'down | 'left | 'right | 'horizontal | 'vertical | 'all } ][ ?depth { 0 ... INT_MAX } ][ ?stopGroup d_stopGroup ][ ?select { t | nil } ])=> ld_instId / nil
functions.description: The traversal can be restricted by providing a maximum traversal depth. A value of 0 or nil indicates no restriction. If an abutment group object is supplied via the ?stopGroup argument, the group is not traversed. The ?select argument, when true, selects the returned instances.

functions.name: lxChain
functions.signature: lxChain(l_instsl_point[ ?groups l_groups ][ ?preserveExistingChains { t | nil } ][ ?useDeviceOrder { t | nil } ][ ?interdigitateChains { t | nil } ][ ?mirror { t | nil } ][ ?permute { t | nil } ][ ?allowSingleBulk { t | nil } ][ ?dummyFlexBothEndNets { t | nil } ][ ?syncChains { t | nil } ][ ?mirrorEquivOrients { t | nil } ][ ?preserveRows { t | nil } ][ ?useAbutSpacing { t | nil } ][ ?maxChainSize x_maxChainSize ][ ?contacts { 0 | 1 | 2 } ][ ?chainAlignPMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ][ ?chainAlignNMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ][ ?chainLeftNet { Source | Drain | Either } ][ ?abutStrategy { sdFirst | dummyFirst } ][ ?optimize { Tracks | Abutments | Both } ][ ?multiRow { NP | PN | NPPN | PNNP } ][ ?effort { Minimal | Nominal | Maximal } ])=> l_chains / nil
functions.description: Chains a list of instances and places the generated chains at the specified position in the layout. Using the optional arguments will override the existing settings of the environment variables: chainPreserveExistingChains, chainUseDeviceOrder, lxAllowPseudoParallelNets, chainMirror, chainPermutePins, chainAllowSingleBulk, chainDummyFlexBothEndNets, chainSyncChains, chainMirrorEquivOrients, chainPreserveRows,chainUseAbutSpacing, lxChainAlignPMOS, lxChainAlignNMOS, chainLeftNet and chainAbutStrategy.

functions.name: lxChainAnchor2D
functions.description: Specifies the pins or instances to be used as anchors to derive connectivity information to chain devices until no further chains can be formed.

functions.name: lxCheck
functions.signature: lxCheck(d_layCV[ ?schCV d_schCV ][ ?checkDevices { t | nil } ][ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ][ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ])=> 0 - 100 / -1
functions.description: Checks the layout for XL compliance and reports binding status in an Info pop-up box. It is recommended to use the lxCheck SKILL function to look for any possible problems in the design if the Navigator XL Status column is not clean. After the issues reported by lxCheck are resolved, running the Connectivity - Update Binding command should give an improved XL Status.

functions.name: lxCheckAgainstSource
functions.signature: lxCheckAgainstSource(d_schCellViewIDd_layCellViewID[ ?masterDiff { t | nil } ][ ?paramDiff { t | nil } ][ ?unboundInsts { t | nil } ][ ?connectivity { t | nil } ][ ?maxDiffsLimit x_maxDiffsLimit ][ ?logFileName t_logFileName ][ ?appendToLog { t | nil } ][ ?nameDiff { t | nil } ][ ?dummyDiff { t | nil } ][ ?busTermDiff { t | nil } ][ ?virtualHierDiff { t | nil } ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Generates a report highlighting the differences between the schematic and the layout cellview. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variable settings in the .cdsenv file.

functions.name: lxCheckAndUpdate
functions.signature: lxCheckAndUpdate(t_libNameOrLayCV[ ?schCV d_schematicCellview ][ ?update g_update ][ ?app t_appName ][ ?layoutComplete g_layoutComplete ][ ?binder t_binderValue ][ ?svdbPath t_lvsSvdbPath ][ ?svdbScale n_lvsScale ][ ?extract g_Extract ][ ?extractStopLevel n_stoplevel) } ][ ?onlyCheckUpdate g_onlyCheckUpdate ][ ?allCellsInDesign g_allCellsInDesign ][ ?allCellsInLibrary g_allCellsInLibrary ][ ?excludeCells t_excludeCells ][ ?includeCells t_includeCells ][ ?leafCells t_leafCells ][ ?withoutSchematic g_cellsWithoutSchematic ][ ?filterMessage l_filterMessage ][ ?createHTML g_createHTMLReport ][ ?openHTML g_openHTMLReport ][ ?logFile g_logFile ][ ?logFileDirectory t_logFileDirectoryPath ][ ?detailedReturn g_detailedReturn ][ ?report { t | nil } ][ ?reportOptions { t| nil } ][ ?graphical { t| nil } ][ ?targetWindow { w_windowId | nil } ])=> nil | l_testResult | n_percentageClean
functions.description: Runs the application readiness check and updates the specified cellviews for the specified applications.

functions.name: lxCheckAndUpdateRegister
functions.signature: lxCheckAndUpdateRegister(t_appNameg_pathg_checkg_update[ ?severity t_severity ][ ?object t_objectType ][ ?checkFunction t_checkFunction ][ ?updateFunction t_updateFunction ][ ?configCB t_arcCallBackFunction ][ ?master g_callCheckUpdateMaster ][ ?subMaster g_callCheckUpdateSubmaster ][ ?markers g_createMarkers ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Registers any user-defined SKILL check and update functions needed for the application readiness check.

functions.name: lxCheckAndUpdateRemove
functions.description: Removes the specified application or test from the application readiness checks.

functions.name: lxCheckAndUpdateSet
functions.signature: lxCheckAndUpdateSet(t_appNameg_path?check g_check?update g_update?severity g_severity)=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets check, update, and severity values for the Application Readiness Checker form.

functions.name: lxCheckLib
functions.signature: lxCheckLib(libName[ ?checkBindings { t | nil } ][ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ][ ?summaryLogFileName t_summaryLogFileName ][ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ])=> 0 - 100 / -1
functions.description: Checks the layouts in the specified library for opens and shorts when extracted to extractStopLevel, and displays the results in CIW and in the Info window. CAD engineers are advised to run this SKILL function to identify the instances that are likely to cause issues with Update Binding.

functions.name: lxCmdOptions
functions.description: Implements a command option for the listed Virtuoso Layout Suite XL commands when the right-mouse button bindkey is pressed. For other Layout XL commands, the right-mouse button bindkey performs the operations as supported by cmdOptions.

functions.name: lxCmdShiftOptions
functions.description: Activates the bindkeys associated with Shift-click and Shift-right click during the operation of enterFunction commands. Typing this command in the Command Interpreter Window has no effect.

functions.name: lxComputeViaParams
functions.signature: lxComputeViaParams(d_viaDefIDd_objID[ ds_constraintGroup ][ l_params ][ f_pathWidth1 ][ t_pathDirection1 ][ f_pathWidth2 ][ t_pathDirection2 ][ l_options ])=> list_of_params | nil
functions.description: Returns a list of DRC-correct via parameters for a specified standard via definition or a custom via definition that references either a cdsVia or a correctly-defined syEnhContact. The via parameters returned are: n_cutWidth, n_cutHeight, l_cutSpacing (X and Y), l_layer1Enc and l_layer2Enc (top, bottom, left, and right).

functions.name: lxConvertSlotToPolygon
functions.signature: lxConvertSlotToPolygon([ ?all { t | nil } ][ ?region l_region ][ ?layers l_layers ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Converts the metal shapes on the drawing purpose to one slotted metal polygon by creating holes where the slot purpose shapes cover the original metal shapes. The original metal shapes and the slot purpose shapes are removed.

functions.name: lxCreateBndFile
functions.signature: lxCreateBndFile([ t_ixfFile ][ t_netFile ][ t_bndFile ][ d_layId ][ g_graphical ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a binding file based on the PVS instance cross-reference file and the extracted netlist file.

functions.name: lxCreateGroupArray
functions.signature: lxCreateGroupArray(d_cvIdl_figList[ ?name t_name ][ ?rows x_rows ][ ?columns x_cols ][ ?X x_xValue ][ ?Y x_yValue ][ ?orients l_orientList ][ ?mode 'pitch | 'spacing ][ ?lpp l_refLPP ])=> d_groupArrayId / nil
functions.description: Creates a group array with the specified parameters.

functions.name: lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups
functions.signature: lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups(( figGroupList )[ dumpConsistencyCheckMsg ][ dumpNonClonableFigGroups ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a new clone family from a list of basic figGroups. When the clone family is created, the function runs the Clone Consistency Checker to verify that the figGroups are effectively synchronous. The checks that are run include verifying that the figGroups are identical, which means their shapes exist on the same layer, instances belong to the same master, and have the same relative position, and so on.

functions.name: lxDeleteSchematicDummies
functions.signature: lxDeleteSchematicDummies([ ?schCV d_schCellViewID ][ ?layCV d_layCellViewID ][ ?layInsts l_insts ][ ?useMFactor { t | nil } ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Deletes bound back annotated schematic instances for the specified dummy layout instances. For mfactored layout devices that have all the layout dummies included in the layout selected set, the SKILL function deletes the schematic dummy instances corresponding to the layout dummies. If all the layout dummy instances of the mfactored device are not included in the selected set, the SKILL function decrements the mfactor to reflect the removal of the selected dummies.

functions.name: lxDeleteSynchronousCloneFamily
functions.description: Deletes the specified family of synchronous clones. As a result, the member clones are desynchronized and they behave as basic groups.

functions.name: lxDeleteVirtualPins
functions.description: Deletes all virtual pins from selected virtual hierarchies.

functions.name: lxDressingTemplateEditor
functions.description: Invokes the Dressing Template Editor form.

functions.name: lxEditPinPlacement
functions.description: Opens the Pin Placement form in which you can view pin information, constrain a pin to a boundary edge, order and fix pins, specify the pitch for pin placement, and start the Pin Placement function.

functions.name: lxEditPlacementStyle
functions.description: Opens the Placement Planning form in which you can plan the placement of CMOS, standard cells, or a mixture of CMOS and standard cells. Each of the three modes generates rows based on the parameters you enter in the form.

functions.name: lxFold
functions.signature: lxFold(l_instsl_pointx_numFolds[ ?widths l_widths ][ ?chainFolds { t | nil } ][ ?ignoreMFactor { t | nil } ][ ?chainAlignPMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ][ ?chainAlignNMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ][ ?enforceWidthMatch { t | nil } ][ ?keepFolds { t | nil } ])=> l_chains / nil
functions.description: Folds a list of valid instances into the specified number of folds and places them at the specified location. If the disableFolding environment variable is set and the folding threshold for the component type is set to 0, folding is disabled.

functions.name: lxGenFromSource
functions.signature: lxGenFromSource(d_schCellViewID[ ?layLibName t_layLibName ][ ?layCellName t_layCellName ][ ?layViewName t_layViewName ][ ?configLib t_configLib ][ ?configCell t_configCell ][ ?configView t_configView ][ ?initCreateInstances { t | nil } ][ ?initDoStacking { t | nil } ][ ?initDoFolding { t | nil } ][ ?initCreatePins { t | nil } ][ ?initGlobalNetPins { t | nil } ][ ?initCreatePadPins { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateBoundary { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateSnapBoundary { t | nil } ][ ?lxPositionMinSep n_lxPositionMinSep ][ ?lxGenerateInBoundary { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateMTM { t | nil } ][ ?extractAfterGenerateAll { t | nil } ][ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ][ ?ignoreSchematicCheck { t | nil } ][ ?initPrBoundaryShape t_initPrBoundaryShape ][ ?initPrBoundaryOrigin l_initPrBoundaryOrigin ][ ?initPrBoundaryPoints l_initPrBoundaryPoints ][ ?initAreaSource1 t_initAreaSource1 ][ ?areaCalc t_areaCalc ][ ?initAreaSource2 t_initAreaSource2 ][ ?initAreaSource1Val n_initAreaSource1Val ][ ?initAreaSource2Val n_initAreaSource2Val ][ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ][ ?softBlocks { t | nil } ][ ?softBlockArea { t | nil } ][ ?useAreaBoundaryUtilization { t | nil } ][ ?areaBoundaryEnclosure n_areaBoundaryEnclosure ][ ?allAreaBoundaries { t | nil } ])=> dbCellViewID
functions.description: Generates a layout from a specified schematic cellview. If you do not specify the layout library, cell, and view names, the layout view is created with the same name as the schematic cell. If you do not specify the physConfig library, cell and view names, the layout view is created with the same name as the layout cell with physConfig as the default physConfigView. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variables set in the .cdsenv file.

functions.name: lxGenerateFinish
functions.description: Finishes the layout generation process by executing the Generate All From Source command with the form values supplied by lxSet* functions and after the previous call to lxGenerateStart.

functions.name: lxGenerateStart
functions.description: Starts the Generate All From Source command, building the Generate Layout form without displaying it to the screen.

functions.name: lxGetAvailablePinLPPs
functions.description: Lists the valid layer-purpose pairs to use for setting the pin layer. This function must always be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish. It is typically used to find a layer-purpose pair to pass to lxSetNetPinSpecs.

functions.name: lxGetCloneFamilyName
functions.description: Returns the family name of the specified clone.

functions.name: lxGetConnRef
functions.description: Gets the connectivity reference for the specified layout cellview or for the layout cellview opened in the specified window. The layout cellview does not need to be open in a Layout XL session for the connectivity reference to be returned.

functions.name: lxGetEditedSyncClone
functions.description: Returns the database ID of the synchronous clone currently being edited in the specified layout cellview. If the function finds a currently-edited layout group which is not a synchronous clone, it recursively checks to determine if its parent group is a synchronous clone. If it is, the function returns the ID of the parent synchronous clone.

functions.name: lxGetGroupArrayParams
functions.description: Returns parameters of the specified group array.

functions.name: lxGetOtherClonesInFamily
functions.description: The generated list does not contain the specified clone.

functions.name: lxGetPermutedInstTerms
functions.description: Returns the list of database IDs of instance terminals that have been permuted on a specified layout instance. The function can identify instance terminals that have been permuted, even if there is no permuteRule property on the schematic or layout instances or their masters.

functions.name: lxGetPinNets
functions.description: Lists the pin net names from the Generate Layout or Update Components and Nets form. This function must always be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish. It is typically used to find net names to pass to lxSetNetPinSpecs.

functions.name: lxGetSchematic
functions.description: Returns either the schematic currently open in an existing Layout XL session, the schematic defined by the connectivity reference returned by lxGetConnRef, or the schematic in the same library and cell as the layout when no connectivity reference is defined.

functions.name: lxGetSource
functions.description: Returns the source (schematic) cellview ID for the specified layout window ID or layout cellview ID in the current Layout XL session. If the schematic reference for the specified layout window has changed since the current Layout XL session was started, Layout XL must be relaunched for lxGetSource to return the updated schematic reference.

functions.name: lxGetSyncClone
functions.description: Returns the database ID of the synchronous clone to which the specified object belongs. If the object belongs to a layout group which is not a synchronous clone, the function recursively checks to determine if its parent group is a synchronous clone. If it is, the function returns the ID of the parent synchronous clone.

functions.name: lxGetValidViaDefs
functions.signature: lxGetValidViaDefs(d_objID[ ds_constraintGroup ][ ltx_bottomLayer ][ ltx_topLayer ])=> list_of_viaDefs / nil
functions.description: Returns a list of via definitions associated with a specified design object. You can restrict the list to include only vias defined in a specified constraint group or which feature a specific top and/or bottom layer. If you specify a technology file, no constraint groups, and no layers, the function returns all the via definitions in the technology database. If you specify both top and bottom layers, the function returns only via definitions featuring those layers. If you specify either a top or bottom layer, the function returns only via definitions featuring the layer in question.

functions.name: lxGetVirtualFigGroupMasterName
functions.description: Returns the schematic cellview name for the specified virtual figGroup in the format 'lib/cell/view'.

functions.name: lxGroupArrayCreatePreset
functions.description: Creates an orientation pattern for group arrays.

functions.name: lxHiAbout
functions.description: Opens the product information window for Layout XL, which includes the release number and the copyright information.

functions.name: lxHiAdjustAreaBoundary
functions.description: Opens the Adjust Boundary form, which can be used to modify the area boundary of the selected virtual figGroups.

functions.name: lxHiAdjustBoundary
functions.description: Adjusts the area boundary of the selected virtual figGroups or the PR Boundary of the selected soft blocks.

functions.name: lxHiAlign
functions.description: Opens the Align form, in which you can specify how selected objects are to be aligned in the layout window design area.

functions.name: lxHiAutoPlace
functions.description: Opens the Auto Placer form in which you can set placement parameters and run the Virtuoso Custom Digital Placer automatic placement function.

functions.name: lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies
functions.signature: lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies([ ?schCV d_schCellViewId ][ ?layCV d_layCellViewId ][ ?autoSchExtract { t | nil } ])=> t
functions.description: Backannotates to schematic the symbols of all the active dummy devices-dummy devices that are not tied to a power or ground net and are not bound in the current layout view. If the schematic and the layout cellview IDs are not supplied, Virtuoso tries to determine them automatically.

functions.name: lxHiBackAnnotateDummies
functions.description: Launches the interactive backannotation enter function to create dummy instances from the layout view into the corresponding schematic view.

functions.name: lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies
functions.signature: lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies([ ?schCV d_schCellViewId ][ ?layCV d_layCellViewId ][ ?autoSchExtract { t | nil } ][ ?figs l_figs ])=> t
functions.description: Backannotates to schematic the symbols of selected active dummy devices-dummy devices that are not tied to a power or ground net and are not bound in the current layout view. If the schematic and the layout cellview IDs are not supplied, Virtuoso tries to determine them automatically.

functions.name: lxHiChain
functions.description: Opens the Generate Chained Devices form, which you can use to specify the transistors in the design to be chained, and starts the interactive chaining function on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, it operates on the design in the current window.

functions.name: lxHiCheck
functions.description: Checks XL compliance of the layout when called using the Connectivity - Check - XL Compliance command.

functions.name: lxHiCheckAllTerminalInterfaces
functions.description: Checks the interface and physical-only status of all the scalar terminals in the currently edited layout cellview. Markers are created in the layout for any mismatches found.

functions.name: lxHiClone
functions.description: Opens the Generate Clones form, which you can use to specify cloning parameters, and starts the interactive cloning function, which lets you replicate a section of the layout in such a way that the new piece of layout material can be placed at more than one location, with each part preserving the hierarchical structure and connectivity of the source. You can clone devices, pins, and (if selected from the layout window) interconnect structures such as wires and paths made of shapes. The interactive cloning function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the design in the current window.

functions.name: lxHiConnectInstPin
functions.description: Opens the Assign Nets form and starts the Assign Nets command, which let you assign instance pins to nets in the design.

functions.name: lxHiConvertMosaicToGroupArray
functions.description: Converts the selected mosaic to a group array. If a mosaic is not selected in the window, it starts the command and prompts you to select the mosaic that you want to convert to a group array.

functions.name: lxHiCreateGroup
functions.description: Creates a figGroup using the selected set of components, if the selected set is not already inside an existing figGroup. If the selected set is inside a virtual hierarchy in a cellview opened in Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL, the SKILL function creates a virtual group.

functions.name: lxHiCreateInstFromSch
functions.description: Opens the Generate Selected Components form and starts the interactive command which lets you generate selected schematic components in the layout view. The function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the current window.

functions.name: lxHiCreateMPP
functions.description: Opens the Create Multipart Path form, which you can use to specify the parameters for creating a multipart path, and starts the interactive command which lets you create a path in the layout window. The function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the design in the current window.

functions.name: lxHiCreatePinsFromLabels
functions.description: Creates pins in the layout from labels for those schematic terminals that do not have a corresponding layout pin. Additionally, creates pins for terminals that already have pins but labels are swapped in the layout.

functions.name: lxHiCreateVirtGroup
functions.description: Creates a virtual figGroup using the selected layout instances that are bound to schematic instances in the same design. When the vhSelectionMode environment variable is set to t, the SKILL function also creates virtual figGroups using selected layout devices that are bound to schematic instances from different designs. If a layout window is not specified, the function creates a virtual figGroup in the current window.

functions.name: lxHiDefineDeviceCorr
functions.description: Opens the Define Device Correspondence form, which lets you bind schematic devices to layout devices.

functions.name: lxHiDesignPlanningOptions
functions.description: Opens the Design Planning and Analysis Options form.

functions.name: lxHiEditComponentTypes
functions.description: Opens the Configure Physical Hierarchy window in Component Types mode, which lets you define component types and assign cells to them. The function operates on the design in the specified layout window. If you do not specify a layout window, it operates on the design in the current one; if there is no current layout window, the function exits.

functions.name: lxHiGenerateSelectedFromLayout
functions.description: Starts the Generate Selected From Layout enter function, which lets you generate selected layout components in the corresponding schematic cellview. The layout window from which the components are selected is specified. If the layout window is not specified, the function operates on the current window.

functions.name: lxHiGenerateSelectedVirtualHierarchy
functions.description: Runs the Generate Selected From Source command with the Design Planning - Virtual Hierarchy option selected to generate virtual hierarchies for the selected schematic instances.

functions.name: lxHiGenerateVirtualHierarchy
functions.description: Runs the Generate All From Source command with the Generate - Design Planning - Virtual Hierarchy option selected to generate virtual hierarchies.

functions.name: lxHiIChain
functions.description: Starts the enter function available through the shortcut menu of selected instances, pins, or a group of abutted instances to support incremental interactive chaining. The selected instances, pins, or a single group of abutted objects are considered as anchors to start the chain and the subsequent user-specified points are then used to interactively chain the instances and top-level pins until the Esc key is pressed to stop the function.

functions.name: lxHiLockSelected
functions.description: Sets the placement status of the currently selected objects to locked. Each object is locked at its current location and orientation in the layout view.

functions.name: lxHiMakeCell
functions.description: Opens the Design Planner Make Cell form, which can be used to create a new cellview using the selected virtual hierarchy from the top-cell layout.

functions.name: lxHiMakeVirtualHierarchy
functions.description: Opens the Make Virtual Hierarchy form, which can be used to create a virtual hierarchy at the top-cell level using the selected layout instance.

functions.name: lxHiMoveAutomatically
functions.description: Runs the Place As In Schematic command, which moves all of the components into the design boundary, maintaining the relative positions of the components in the schematic. If there is no connectivity reference, the Update Connectivity Reference form is opened.

functions.name: lxHiPRBoundaryInteriorHalo
functions.description: Displays an options form to specify if and on which layer a PR boundary interior halo shape should be created during when the Generate All From Source command is run.

functions.name: lxHiPlaceBoundaryCell
functions.description: Opens the Boundary Cell Placement form.

functions.name: lxHiPlaceFiller
functions.description: Displays the Insert/Delete Filler Cells form.

functions.name: lxHiProbe
functions.description: Opens the Probe Options form and starts the XL Probe command, which lets you select a component in either the layout or schematic and highlights the corresponding component the other cellview of the pair.

functions.name: lxHiReInitDesign
functions.description: Opens the Generate Layout form, which you can use to specify which layout components are to be generated from the schematic cellview, or clears the existing layout cellview so that you can restart.

functions.name: lxHiRemaster
functions.description: Opens the Remaster form, which can be used to replace the selected virtual hierarchy with an existing layout variant.

functions.name: lxHiSetOptions
functions.description: Opens the Connectivity form. The form opens with the General tab on top, unless you specify a different tab using the optional argument.

functions.name: lxHiSnapPatternOptions
functions.description: Opens the Design Planning and Analysis Options form to create snap pattern grids and specify that horizontal and vertical tracks be created inside the PR boundary.

functions.name: lxHiStack
functions.description: Opens the Generate Folded Devices form and starts the Generate Folded Devices command, which lets you fold a single transistor or an abutted group of MOS transistors into two or more fingers. The command operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, it operates on the design in the current window.

functions.name: lxHiSwap
functions.description: Swaps instances and figGroups by launching the Swapping Components command. You can pre-select, partial-select, or post-select instances and figGroups. You can use the function to swap by origin with an option to swap with transform, or you can select one of the nine points on a bounding box: lower-left, center-left, upper-left, lower-center, center-center, upper-center, lower-right, center-right, or upper-right.

functions.name: lxHiUnlockSelected
functions.description: Changes the placement status of the selected objects from locked, placed, or firm to unplaced.If the original placement status is unknown or unplaced, this command does not change it.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateAllTerminalInterfaces
functions.description: Updates the scalar terminals in the currently edited layout cellview to correct mismatches in the interface or physical-only status.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateBinding
functions.description: Displays the Update Binding form.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateBusTerminals
functions.description: Updates the implicit bus terminals in the layout cellview based on the corresponding explicit bus terminals in the schematic cellview. The update is important to support interoperability of the layout cellviews with the designs created using the Innovus Implementation System.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateCellViewPair
functions.signature: lxHiUpdateCellViewPair([ d_cellviewID ])=> ( { t_source t_lib t_cell t_view [ t_topcell ] | nil } )
functions.description: Starts the Update Connectivity Reference command and opens the Update Connectivity Reference form, where you can specify which schematic view provides the connectivity source for the specified layout view. If you do not specify a layout cellview, the function uses the current layout cellview.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateComponentsAndNets
functions.description: Starts the Update Components and Nets command, which lets you update the devices and pins in the layout view based on the devices in the schematic cellview.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateLayoutConstraints
functions.description: Runs the Update Layout Constraints command, which transfers constraints from the schematic view to the layout view. Constraints that have been created in the schematic but not yet saved are also transferred. Constraints are transferred only to the top-level layout view and are made read-only.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateLayoutParameters
functions.description: Starts the Update Layout Parameters command, which updates the parameters and values in the layout view to match those set in the schematic view.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateSchematicParameters
functions.description: Starts the Update Schematic Parameters command, which updates the parameters and values in the schematic view to match those set in the layout view.

functions.name: lxHiUpdateTerminalNetExpressions
functions.description: Corrects mismatches in the terminal net expressions between layout and schematic reported by the Check Against Source command.

functions.name: lxHiVerifyDesign
functions.description: Starts the Check Against Source command and opens the Check Against Source dialog where you can specify how Layout XL is to check the current layout implementation against corresponding schematic view. When you accept the dialog, the command checks the schematic cellview for any changes made since the layout cellview was last changed. It also opens an Info window detailing the differences between the views.

functions.name: lxHiVirtHierOptions
functions.description: Opens the Design Planning and Analysis Options form, which can be used to specify whether the layout displays the name of the virtual hierarchy, the cell, or both. In addition, the form can be used to enable or disable symbol overlay and to specify whether the virtual hierarchy can be auto placed during editing.

functions.name: lxHierCheck
functions.signature: lxHierCheck(layCV[ ?checkDevices { t | nil } ][ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ][ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ][ ?hierSummaryLogFileName t_hierSummaryLogFileName ])=> 0 - 100 / -1
functions.description: Arguments

functions.name: lxHierCheckAgainstSource
functions.signature: lxHierCheckAgainstSource(d_layCellViewID[ ?masterDiff { t | nil } ][ ?paramDiff { t | nil } ][ ?unboundInsts { t | nil } ][ ?connectivity { t | nil } ][ ?maxDiffsLimit x_maxDiffsLimit ][ ?logFileName t_logFileName ][ ?appendToLog { t | nil } ][ ?nameDiff { t | nil } ][ ?dummyDiff { t | nil } ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Generates a report highlighting the differences between the schematic and layout cellviews for unique layout masters in the specified layout hierarchy. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variables set in the .cdsenv file. This SKILL function always skips any layouts that have no instances. If a log file name is specified for the hierSummaryLogFileName environment variable, the SKILL function prints the summary information to the specified log file, in addition to printing the information to the default Virtuoso log file.

functions.name: lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets
functions.signature: lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets(d_layCellViewID[ ?initCreatePins { t | nil } ][ ?initGlobalNetPins { t | nil } ][ ?initCreatePadPins { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateInstances { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateBoundary { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateSnapBoundary { t | nil } ][ ?initDoStacking { t | nil } ][ ?initDoFolding { t | nil } ][ ?initCreateMTM { t | nil } ][ ?deleteUnmatchedInsts { t | nil } ][ ?deleteUnmatchedPins { t | nil } ][ ?updateReplacesMasters { t | nil } ][ ?updateWithMarkers { t | nil } ][ ?updateLayoutParameters { t | nil } ][ ?updateNetSigType { t | nil } ][ ?updateNetMinMaxVoltage { t | nil } ][ ?updateNetsOnly { t | nil } ][ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ][ ?skipLeafs { t | nil } ][ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Updates the components and nets for all unique layout masters in the specified layout cellview hierarchy. The layouts are automatically opened in edit mode for update. If a log file name is specified for the hierSummaryLogFileName environment variable, the SKILL function prints the summary information to the specified log file, in addition to printing the information to the default Virtuoso log file.

functions.name: lxIsGroupArray
functions.description: Checks whether the given object is a group array.

functions.name: lxIsGroupArrayEnabled
functions.description: Checks whether the group array functionality is available.

functions.name: lxIsGroupArrayLocked
functions.description: Checks whether the given group array is locked.

functions.name: lxIsGroupArrayRegular
functions.description: Checks whether the given group array is a regular group array. For a regular group array, the number of cells can be modified by updating the number of rows or columns. For a non-regular group array, the number of cells is fixed.

functions.name: lxIsVirtualFigGroup
functions.description: Checks if the specified figGroup is a virtual figGroup.

functions.name: lxLaunchLayoutEXL
functions.description: Launches Layout EXL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout EXL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

functions.name: lxLaunchLayoutMXL
functions.description: Launches Layout MXL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout MXL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

functions.name: lxLaunchLayoutXL
functions.description: Launches Layout XL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout XL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

functions.name: lxMakeDummy
functions.description: Starts the Make Dummy enter function for the selected set of instances which can include mosaics. The function requires a reference point and a position for the created dummy devices. The dummy devices are tied to the named net passed in via netName.

functions.name: lxMakePrBoundarySelectable
functions.description: Makes the place and route boundary in the current layout selectable.

functions.name: lxMakePrBoundaryUnselectable
functions.description: Makes the place and route boundary in the current layout unselectable.

functions.name: lxMakeVirtualHierarchy
functions.signature: lxMakeVirtualHierarchy(d_layCellViewIDl_insts[ ?allInstsSameMaster { t | nil } ][ ?preserveVirtualPins { t | nil } ][ ?keepLabels { t | nil } ][ ?placementStatus { Fixed | Locked | None } ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates virtual hierarchies from the cells of the listed bound instances.

functions.name: lxMovePorts
functions.description: Moves top-level ports over components based on their connectivity.

functions.name: lxPermPermutePins
functions.description: Starts the Permute Pins command, which lets you swap the connectivity or net connections of the pins of a component. You specify the pins you want to permute by selecting them when prompted by the function. The pins to be permuted must belong to different nets and must first be defined as permutable terminals using the permuteRule property for the device.

functions.name: lxProbeRemoveAll
functions.description: Removes all probes from the layout cellview.

functions.name: lxRegMasterDiffName
functions.description: Registers a SKILL function that can return a name for the master difference reported by the Check Against Source command.

functions.name: lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNets
functions.description: Registers a SKILL function to be used as a post-function hook for lxUpdateComponentsAndNets to enable replacement of pins that have their layer and width characteristics defined using the Design Intent tool. lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, when used in combination with lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, avoids the need for deleting the pins defined in Design Intent before the pins can be updated.

functions.name: lxRegPrePosition
functions.description: Registers a SKILL function for a schematic Pcell to be called for newly generated layout instances corresponding to each instance of the schematic Pcell when Generate All From Source, Generate Selected from Source, or Update Components and Nets commands are run. Registration is done once before generation. The registered SKILL function is called after instance generation but before positioning.Only one SKILL function can be registered per schematic Pcell.

functions.name: lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNets
functions.description: Registers a SKILL function to be used as a pre-function hook for lxUpdateComponentsAndNets to enable replacement of pins that have their layer and width characteristics defined using the Design Intent tool. lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, when used in combination with lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, avoids the need for deleting the pins defined in Design Intent before the pins can be updated.

functions.name: lxRemoveSynchronousCloneFromFamily
functions.description: Removes a specified synchronous clone from its family. As a result, the clone is desynchronized and it behaves as a basic group. If a clone that belongs to a two-member synchronous family is removed from the family, the other member clone is also removed and the family is deleted.

functions.name: lxRunCmdInVXL
functions.description: This function is being maintained only to support backward compatibility. Cadence recommends that you use lxRunCmdInXL instead.
