functions.name: prms
functions.description: Computes the periodic root mean square of a family of signals for each time point, which is the square root of the periodic average of the square of the input waveform.

functions.name: probeTrigger

This trigger allows the probing mechanism to keep its data structures consistent without requiring each application to call it separately.

functions.name: procedure
functions.description: Defines a function using a formal argument list. The body of the procedure is a list of expressions to evaluate.

functions.name: procedurep
functions.description: Checks if an object is a procedure, or function, object.

functions.name: profileReset

functions.name: progn

functions.description: Returns the dimensions of the specified paper size.

functions.description: Returns the paper sizes (such as A size) and offset of the paper that the plotter uses.

functions.name: psQueryPlotters
functions.description: Returns a list of plotter names from the loaded .cdsplotinit files.

functions.name: psQueueStatus
functions.description: Displays the plot jobs in the spooling queues.

functions.name: psd
functions.signature: psd(o_waveformf_timeStartf_timeEndx_num[ ?windowName t_windowName ][ ?smooth x_smooth ][ ?cohGain f_cohGain ][ ?windowsize x_windowsize ][ ?detrending t_detrending ])=> o_waveformReal / nil
functions.description: Returns an estimate for the power spectral density of o_waveform. If x_windowsize is not a power of 2, it is forced to the next higher power of 2. If x_num is less than x_windowsize, x_num is forced to x_windowsize.

functions.name: psdbb
functions.signature: psdbb(o_waveform1o_waveform2f_timeStartf_timeEndx_num[ ?windowName t_windowName ][ ?smooth x_smooth ][ ?cohGain f_cohGain ][ ?windowsize x_windowsize ][ ?detrending t_detrending ])=> o_waveformReal / nil
functions.description: Returns an estimate for the power spectral density of o_waveform1+j*o_waveform2. If x_windowsize is not a power of 2, it is forced to the next higher power of 2. If x_num is less than x_windowsize, x_num is forced to x_windowsize.

functions.name: pstddev
functions.description: Computes the periodic standard deviation of a family of signals for each time point.

functions.name: pteCancelForm
functions.description: Closes the specified Palette form.

functions.name: pteClearSearchHistory
functions.description: Clears the search history for the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteCloseLayerSetEdition
functions.description: Closes layer set editing mode for the specified window, or for the current window if no window ID is specified.

functions.name: pteCloseMPTSupportMode
functions.description: Hides the MPT-support-related Palette UI options.

functions.name: pteCollapse
functions.description: Collapses the specified item in the specified Palette panel in the specified window.

functions.name: pteCollapseAll
functions.description: Collapses all items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteContextMenu
functions.description: Displays the contextual menu for the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteDeleteLayerSet
functions.description: Deletes the specified layer set and the corresponding layer set file.

functions.name: pteDeselect
functions.description: Deselects an individual item in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteDeselectAll
functions.description: Deselects all items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteDiscardLayerSetEdition
functions.description: Discards the changes made to the validity or membership state of a layer-purpose pair during the current layer set editing session.

functions.name: pteDockWindow
functions.description: Docks the specified Palette assistant.

functions.name: pteEditLayerSet
functions.description: Enables addition or deletion of layer-purpose pairs in a layer set.

functions.name: pteEditLayerSetValidity
functions.description: Enables you to edit the validity and membership state of layer-purpose pairs in the selected layer sets.

functions.name: pteExpand
functions.description: Expands the specified item in the specified Palette panel in the specified window.

functions.name: pteExpandAll
functions.description: Expands all objects in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteExportLayerSet
functions.description: Exports a layer set from a Palette layer set repository to the file system.

functions.name: pteFindNext
functions.description: Finds and sets as active the next layer-purpose pair that matches the search string, in the specified panel. This function works only if the Search Mode option in the Palette Options form is set to Filter.

functions.name: pteFindPrev
functions.description: Finds and sets as active the previous layer-purpose pair that matches the search string, in the specified panel. This function works only if the Search Mode option in the Palette Options form is set as Filter.

functions.name: pteGetActiveScopeModes
functions.description: Returns a list containing the scope modes that are set as active in the specified window.

functions.name: pteGetAllActiveLayerSets
functions.description: Returns a list containing the layer sets that are set as active in the design open in the specified window.

functions.name: pteGetAllLayerSets
functions.description: Returns a list containing all the layer sets available in the design open in the specified window.

functions.name: pteGetCurrentPanel
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the currently active Palette panel.

functions.name: pteGetLPPDisplayedInPalette
functions.description: Lists the layer-purpose pairs currently displayed in the Layers panel.

functions.name: pteGetLSAtPosition
functions.description: Displays the name of the layer set that is listed at the specified position in the Layer Set Manager.

functions.name: pteGetLayerPath
functions.description: Retrieves the element path of the specified layer-purpose pair when the View By mode is applied to the Palette. The result can be used to provide the t_paletteElementPath argument needed by the pteSetVisible, pteSetSelectability, pteSetValidity, pteSetOnlyVisible, pteSetOnlySelectable, ptePropagateVisibility, and ptePropagateSelectability functions in the View By mode.

functions.name: pteGetLayerSetColoredLpp
functions.description: Returns the layer-purpose pair associated with the specified layer set.

functions.name: pteGetLayerSetMembers
functions.description: Returns the attribute settings for layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids that are members of the specified layer set. For layer-purpose pairs, attributes include visibility, selectability, validity, priority, and routing direction (if set). For objects, attributes include visibility and selectability; and for grids, the attribute returned is visibility.

functions.name: pteGetMPTSupportMode
functions.description: Determines if MPT support is enabled in the window with the specified ID.

functions.name: pteGetNextLayerSets
functions.description: Returns the layer set listed immediately below the layer set if only one layer set is selected in the Layer Set Manager. If multiple layer sets are selected in the Layer Set Manager, returns a list comprising layer sets listed immediately below each selected layer set.

functions.name: pteGetPrevLayerSets
functions.description: Returns the layer set listed immediately above the layer set if only one layer set is selected in the Layer Set Manager. If multiple layer sets are selected in the Layer Set Manager, returns a list comprising layer sets listed immediately above each selected layer set.

functions.name: pteGetSelection
functions.description: Retrieves a list of the selected layer-purpose pairs, objects, or grids from the specified panel.

functions.name: pteHideAllTools
functions.description: Hides all Palette tools and toolbars.

functions.name: pteImportLayerSet
functions.description: Imports the specified layer set file from the file system to the Palette repository and saves it with the specified name.

functions.name: pteInfraGetPaletteMode
functions.description: Returns the container type of the Palette that is currently active.

functions.name: pteIsSelectable
functions.signature: pteIsSelectable({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Retrieves the selectability state for the specified layer-purpose pair or object.

functions.name: pteIsVisible
functions.signature: pteIsVisible({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Retrieves the visibility state for the specified layer-purpose pair, object, or grid.

functions.name: pteLoadConfig
functions.description: Loads the specified Palette configuration file. A Palette configuration file contains Palette-related information, such as the columns and toolbars to be displayed and their location.

functions.name: pteLoadDefaults
functions.description: Loads the display context with the default values. A display context determines display properties, such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids.

functions.name: pteLoadFromTechFile
functions.description: Loads the display context from the technology file into the Palette. A display context determines display properties such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids.

functions.name: pteLoadGDSNumber
functions.description: Loads the GDS number layermap file from the specified location into the Palette.

functions.name: pteLoadLSWInfo
functions.description: Loads the specified Layer Selection Window (LSW) information file into the Palette. The visibility and selectability settings stored in the LSW information file for layer-purpose pairs and objects are loaded into the Palette.

functions.name: pteLoadLayerSet
functions.description: Loads a layer set from a layer set file existing in a palette repository.

functions.name: pteMPTSupportMode
functions.description: Displays the MPT-support-related Palette UI options.

functions.name: pteMapWindow
functions.description: Displays, if hidden, the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteMinimizeSingleWindowPalette
functions.description: Minimizes the Palette, but only if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

functions.name: pteMoveLayerSelection
functions.description: Moves the layer-purpose pairs selected in the Layers panel to the specified position. This function works only if the View By mode is set to None.

functions.name: pteMoveSingleWindowPalette
functions.description: Places the upper-left corner of the Palette at the specified x- and y-coordinate, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

functions.name: pteOpenForm
functions.description: Displays the specified Palette form.

functions.name: ptePropagateSelectability
functions.signature: ptePropagateSelectability({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_selectabilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Propagates selectability changes to child items when the parent and child items are in a desynchronized state. Specify either t_layerPurposeName or t_paletteElementPath.

functions.name: ptePropagateVisibility
functions.signature: ptePropagateVisibility({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_visibilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Propagates visibility changes to child items when the parent and child items are in a desynchronized state. Specify either t_layerPurposeName or t_paletteElementPath.

functions.name: pteRaiseSingleWindowPalette
functions.description: Places the Palette on top of the other open windows, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

functions.name: pteRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger
functions.description: Registers a trigger, which is a user-defined SKILL procedure, from CIW. This trigger is called with an argument list containing modifier, mouseButton, event, editedLS, and activeLSList when an action (other than a drag-and-drop action) is performed in the Layer Set Manager.

functions.name: pteRegisterUserSelectionTrigger
functions.description: Registers a trigger, which is a user-defined SKILL procedure, from CIW. This trigger is called with an argument list containing windowId, layerName, purposeName, mouseButton, and modifier for every selection action. Valid values for mouseButton are Left, Right, and Middle; valid values for modifier are None, Shift, and Ctrl.

functions.name: pteReloadLayerSet
functions.description: Reloads the layer set file for the layer set that is currently in use. This resynchronizes the visibility and selectability status of the layers, objects, or grids items with that available in the layer set file.

functions.name: pteResizeSingleWindowPalette
functions.description: Resizes the Palette by using the specified width and height values, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

functions.name: pteSaveAsLayerSet
functions.description: Saves the layer set currently in use with a new name.

functions.name: pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet
functions.description: Saves the layer set currently in use, as a synchronized layer set, with the specified name in the specified layer set repository. The newly saved layer set is set as active.

functions.name: pteSaveConfig
functions.description: Saves the Palette configuration information in the specified file. This includes information about the Palette settings, such as the columns and toolbars currently displayed in the Palette.

functions.name: pteSaveGDSNumber
functions.description: Saves the active GDSII number layermap file.

functions.name: pteSaveLSWInfo
functions.description: Saves the current LSW Info file at the specified location. This file contains information about the state of the Palette. It does not store the color and lock information of layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteSaveLayerSet
functions.description: Saves the changes made to the layer set that is currently in use.

functions.name: pteSaveLayerSetList
functions.description: Saves the list of layer sets displayed in the Layer Set Manager to a file named layerset.order. The order in which the layer sets are listed and the enable state of each layer set is also saved.

functions.name: pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository
functions.description: Saves the list of layer sets displayed in the Layer Set Manager to a file named layerset.order in the specified repository. The order in which the layer sets are listed and their state-whether enabled or disabled-is also saved.

functions.name: pteSaveToTechFile
functions.description: Saves the display context from the Palette to the technology file. A display context determines display properties such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids. The display context stored in individual layer sets is not considered.

functions.name: pteSelect
functions.description: Selects the specified layer, object, or grid. An item selected previously is not deselected when you run the command again to select another item. This function works only if the Selection Mode is set to Multi Selection.

functions.name: pteSelectAll
functions.description: Selects all items in the specified Palette panel. This function works only if the Selection Mode is set to Multi Selection.

functions.name: pteSetActiveLpp
functions.description: Sets the specified layer-purpose pair as active. A layer that is not defined in the technology file is not displayed in the Palette, and an invalid layer cannot be set as active. Therefore, ensure that the specified layer is defined in the technology file and is valid.

functions.name: pteSetActiveLppColor
functions.signature: pteSetActiveLppColor({ grayColor | mask1Color | mask2Color }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the specified color for the active layer-purpose pair. The lock state is set to unlocked.

functions.name: pteSetActiveLppColorLock
functions.signature: pteSetActiveLppColorLock({ t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Locks or unlocks the color on the current active layer-purpose pair.

functions.name: pteSetAllLSEnable
functions.description: Enables or disables all the layer sets listed in the Layer Set Manager, except the one that is currently in use.

functions.name: pteSetAllLayerSetMember
functions.signature: pteSetAllLayerSetMember([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets all specified layer-purpose pairs as members of the layer set that is currently in use.

functions.name: pteSetAllSelectable
functions.signature: pteSetAllSelectable([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets as selectable the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetAllStipple
functions.signature: pteSetAllStipple([ ?mode { Display | Selection } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets to visible the stipple for the specified layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteSetAllValidity
functions.signature: pteSetAllValidity([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets as valid the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetAllVisible
functions.signature: pteSetAllVisible([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets as visible the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetBindkeys
functions.description: Opens the Bindkey Editor form to the Palette section, with the Palette bindkeys displayed in the right pane.

functions.name: pteSetConfig
functions.description: Assigns the specified configValue to the configName configuration parameter in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetFindModeOn
functions.description: Toggles the search mode for the specified window between Find and Filter.

functions.name: pteSetLSActive
functions.signature: pteSetLSActive(?layerSets t_layerSets?turnOnVis { t | nil }?turnOnSel { t | nil }?turnOffAllVis { t | nil }?turnOffAllSel { t | nil }?deactivateOthers { t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Activates one or more layer sets and can be used to force the visibility and selectability of the layer-purpose pairs contained in those layer sets. The visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs contained in layer sets previously set as active is affected only if the visibility or selectability of layer-purpose pairs contained in the layer set being set as active is forced.

functions.name: pteSetLSEnable
functions.description: Enables or disables the specified layer set. The layer set currently in use cannot be disabled.

functions.name: pteSetLSPosition
functions.description: Moves the specified layer set to the specified position in the Layer Set Manager.

functions.name: pteSetLSSelectable
functions.description: Turns on or off the selectability state of all the layer-purpose pairs contained in the specified layer set.

functions.name: pteSetLSVisible
functions.description: Turns on or off the visibility state of all the layer-purpose pairs contained in the specified layer set.

functions.name: pteSetLayerSetColoredLpp
functions.description: Sets the layer-purpose pair for the specified layer set.

functions.name: pteSetLayerSetMember
functions.description: Adds or removes the specified layer-purpose pair from the layer set currently in use.

functions.name: pteSetLppVisibleByString
functions.description: Searches for the specified search string based on the advanced search options (casing, match type, and search operator) set in the Layers panel, and sets the visibility state for all layer-purpose pairs that match the search criteria to the specified value.

functions.name: pteSetMPTSupportMode
functions.description: Enables or disables MPT support in the window with the specified ID.

functions.name: pteSetNoneLayerSetMember
functions.signature: pteSetNoneLayerSetMember([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Removes from the active layer set all items that meet the specified criteria.

functions.name: pteSetNoneSelectable
functions.signature: pteSetNoneSelectable([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Turns off the selectability of the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetNoneStipple
functions.signature: pteSetNoneStipple([ ?mode { Display | Selection } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Hides the stipple for the specified layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteSetNoneValidity
functions.signature: pteSetNoneValidity([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets as invalid the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetNoneVisible
functions.signature: pteSetNoneVisible([ ?mode { Display | Selection | Propagate } ][ ?only { t | nil } ][ ?panel { Layers | Objects | Grids } ][ ?window w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets as invisible the specified items in the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteSetOnlySelectable
functions.signature: pteSetOnlySelectable({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Turns on the selectability of the specified item in the specified panel. All other items in the specified panel are made non-selectable.

functions.name: pteSetOnlySelectableWithDepth
functions.signature: pteSetOnlySelectableWithDepth({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Turns on the selectability of the specified layer-purpose pair and of the n layer-purpose pairs listed both above and below the specified layer-purpose pair in the Layers panel. The value n is obtained from the Depth for Selectability field in the Palette Options form. Selectability of all other layer-purpose pairs is turned off.

functions.name: pteSetOnlyVisible
functions.signature: pteSetOnlyVisible({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Turns on the visibility of the specified item in the specified panel. All other items are made invisible.

functions.name: pteSetOnlyVisibleWithDepth
functions.signature: pteSetOnlyVisibleWithDepth({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }t_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Turns on the visibility of the specified layer-purpose pair and of the n layer-purpose pairs listed both above and below the specified layer-purpose pair in the Layers panel. The value n is obtained from the Depth for Visibility field in the Palette Options form. Visibility of all other layer-purpose pairs is turned off.

functions.name: pteSetOption
functions.description: Assigns a value to the specified Palette option.

functions.name: pteSetOptionString
functions.description: Changes the state of a Palette environment variable during a Virtuoso session.

functions.name: pteSetRoutingDirection
functions.description: Sets the routing direction for the specified layer-purpose pair.

functions.name: pteSetSearchMatchCase
functions.description: Specifies whether search is case-sensitive or case-insensitive.

functions.name: pteSetSearchMatchType
functions.description: Limits searches to items that match the search string, items with a specific prefix or suffix, or items that contain the search string as a substring.

functions.name: pteSetSearchOperator
functions.description: Sets the default operator for the search criteria. Valid values are and, or, phrase, and not. Panel name is one of Layers, Objects, or Grids.

functions.name: pteSetSearchText
functions.description: Searches for the specified search string based on the casing, match type, and search operator set for the panel in which the search is to be performed.

functions.name: pteSetSelectable
functions.signature: pteSetSelectable({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_selectabilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the selectability state for the specified item.

functions.name: pteSetShowLockedColors
functions.signature: pteSetShowLockedColors({ t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Displays or hides the colors locked on shapes.

functions.name: pteSetShowUnlockedColors
functions.signature: pteSetShowUnlockedColors({ t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Displays or hides the unlocked colors on shapes.

functions.name: pteSetStipple
functions.signature: pteSetStipple({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_stippleVisibilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the stipple visibility state for the specified layer-purpose pair.

functions.name: pteSetValidity
functions.signature: pteSetValidity({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_validityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the validity state for the specified item.

functions.name: pteSetVisible
functions.signature: pteSetVisible({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_visibilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the visibility state for the specified item.

functions.name: pteSetVisibleWithDepth
functions.signature: pteSetVisibleWithDepth({ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }g_visibilityStatet_panelName[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Sets the visibility for the specified layer-purpose pair and for the n layer-purpose pairs listed both above and below the specified layer-purpose pair in the Layers panel. The value n is obtained from the Depth for Visibility field in the Palette Options form.

functions.name: pteSetWindowSynchro
functions.description: Synchronizes or desynchronizes the Palette.

functions.name: pteShowAllTools

functions.name: pteShowMPTLPP
functions.signature: pteShowMPTLPP({ t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Displays in the Layers panel only those layer-purpose pairs that have color information.

functions.name: pteShowRoutingLPP
functions.description: Displays only the routing layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel.

functions.name: pteShowUsedLPP
functions.description: Displays only the currently used layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel.

functions.name: pteShowValidLPP
functions.description: Displays only valid layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllLayerSetMember
functions.description: Toggles the layer set membership status of all the items in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllSelectable
functions.description: Toggles the selectability status of all the items listed in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllStipple
functions.description: Toggles the stipple visibility status of all the layer-purpose pairs in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllTools
functions.description: Toggles the display status of all toolbars in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllValidity
functions.description: Toggles the validity status of all the items in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleAllVisible
functions.description: Toggles the visibility status of all the items listed in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleLSActive
functions.signature: pteToggleLSActive(?layerSets t_layerSetName[ ?toggleVis { t | nil } ][ ?toggleSel { t | nil } ][ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Adds or removes the specified layer set from the list of active layer sets. Additionally, toggles the visibility and selectability status of the various layer-purpose pairs contained in the layer set.

functions.name: pteToggleLayerSetEdition
functions.description: Displays or hides the membership status of layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteToggleLayerSetValidityEdition
functions.description: Displays or hides the validity and membership status of layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteTogglePanels
functions.description: Displays the contents of the specified panel and hides the other two panels.

functions.name: pteTogglePropagateAllSelectable
functions.description: Toggles the selectability status of all parent and child items in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteTogglePropagateAllVisible
functions.description: Toggles the visibility status of all parent and child items in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleShowMPTLPP
functions.description: Toggles the display of layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel between all layer-purpose pairs and layer-purpose pairs with color information.

functions.name: pteToggleShowRoutingLPP
functions.description: Toggles the display of layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel between routing layer-purpose pairs and all layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteToggleShowUsedLPP
functions.description: Toggles the display of layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel between currently used layer-purpose pairs and all layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteToggleShowValidLPP
functions.description: Toggles the display of layer-purpose pairs in the Layers panel between valid layer-purpose pairs and all layer-purpose pairs.

functions.name: pteToggleToolbars
functions.description: Toggles the display status of all toolbars in the specified panel.

functions.name: pteToggleWindowSynchro
functions.description: Synchronizes or desynchronizes the Palette.

functions.name: pteUnRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger
functions.description: Unregisters the SKILL procedure that was registered using pteRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger.

functions.name: pteUnRegisterUserSelectionTrigger
functions.description: Unregisters the SKILL procedure that was registered using pteRegisterUserSelectionTrigger.

functions.name: pteUndockWindow
functions.description: Undocks the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteUnmapWindow
functions.description: Unmaps (hides, if displayed) the specified Palette panel.

functions.name: pteUnsetLSActive
functions.signature: pteUnsetLSActive(?layerSets t_layerSets?turnOffAllVis { t | nil }?turnOffAllSel { t | nil }[ w_windowId ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Deactivates one or more layer sets and can be used to force the visibility and selectability of the layer-purpose pairs contained in those layer sets.

functions.name: pushf

functions.name: putc
functions.description: Puts the x_symbol to p_port (to complement getc function)

functions.name: putd
functions.description: Assigns a new function binding, which must be a function, a lambda expression, or nil, to a function name. If you just want to define a function, use procedure or defun.

functions.name: putprop

functions.name: rdeReplay

This is in contrast to rdeSource, in which the entire Tcl file is read into the interpreter and then executed. It may be useful in determining which line of a script file had an error, in case an error occurs. Since each line is executed independently, it is not possible to create expressions (such as function definitions) that span more than one line.

Otherwise, the SKILL path would be searched first for S_old. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

functions.description: Adds a number to the Y coordinate of l_point and returns the resulting point as l_point.

functions.signature: rodAlign([ ?alignObj R_alignObj ][ ?alignHandle S_alignHandle ][ ?refObj R_refObj ][ ?refHandle S_refHandle ][ ?refPoint l_refPoint ][ ?maintain g_maintain ][ ?xSep txf_xSep ][ ?ySep txf_ySep ]);end rodAlign=> R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Aligns a named object by a point handle on that object to a specific point or to a point handle on a reference object. You can align objects that are at different levels of hierarchy as long as both objects are in the same top-level layout cellview. You can specify positive or negative separation between alignment points in the direction of both the X and Y axes, either as absolute distances or with Cadence SKILL language expressions. The system applies the offset from the reference point or reference object to the object to be aligned.

functions.name: rodAssignHandleToParameter
functions.signature: rodAssignHandleToParameter([ ?parameter S_parameter ][ ?rodObj R_rodObj ][ ?handleName Sl_handleName ][ ?displayName S_displayName ][ ?displayExpression S_displayExpression ][ ?stretchDir S_stretchDir ][ ?stretchType S_stretchType ][ ?moveOrigin g_moveOrigin ][ ?updateIncrement f_updateIncrement ][ ?userData g_userData ][ ?userFunction Sl_userFunction ][ ?stretchKey S_stretchKey ][ ?shape S_shape ]);end rodAssignHandleToParameter=> t / nil
functions.description: Assigns one or more user- or system-defined point handles on a ROD object within a SKILL-based parameterized cell (Pcell) to a single Pcell parameter, so you can change the value of the parameter by graphically stretching the handle(s). Stretching a handle has the same effect as changing the value of the associated parameter for the Pcell instance using the Edit Properties form. You cannot stretch handles on the Pcell master. All rodAssignHandleToParameter statements must occur within the body-of-code section of a SKILL-based Pcell.

functions.name: rodCheck
functions.description: Searches the specified cellview for multipart paths (MPPs) for which the geometry does not match the definition information, and returns a list of the ROD object IDs. The MPPs found by this function include those that have lost their subshape definition information. By default, this function places warning markers over the potentially affected MPPs. (If you do not want to see warning markers, set the g_createMarkers argument to nil.) Although subparts with missing definition information are still visible graphically, their definitions have been deleted from the database. Editing an affected MPP causes an immediate loss of the subpart graphics.

functions.name: rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView
functions.description: Finds and opens the design specified by t_libName, t_cellName, and t_viewName, and checks if any MPP in the design contains defective internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView fixes them and creates markers on them depending on the values of g_fix and g_createMarkers arguments.

functions.name: rodCheckMPPs
functions.description: Checks if the given list of multipart paths (MPPs) contains corrupt internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckMPPs fixes or creates markers to highlight them, or does both.

functions.name: rodCoordBisect
functions.description: Divides the input value by two (bisect). You can optionally set the argument that rounds off the calculated value, truncates it, or converts it based on the defined maximum ceiling.

functions.name: rodCoordCreate
functions.signature: rodCoordCreate(g_inputValue [ S_unitType [ S_snapType ] ][ x_resolution ]);end rodCoordCreate=> o_rodCoordObj
functions.description: Creates a rodCoord object from the given value, that is, g_inputValue.

functions.name: rodCoordDefineGrid
functions.description: Defines the grid and the arithmetic resolution factor values, which are used by the rodCoord* API.

functions.name: rodCoordFix
functions.description: Fixes the rodCoord object and returns a new rodCoord object using the fix() SKILL function.

functions.name: rodCoordGetGrid
functions.description: Returns the grid value (defined by rodCoordDefineGrid) as a rodCoord object.

functions.name: rodCoordIsOnGrid
functions.description: Checks if the data in the given rodCoord object is on the grid or not.

functions.name: rodCoordParseString
functions.description: Creates a rodCoord object out of t_rodString generated by the rodCoordToString function.

functions.name: rodCoordPartition
functions.description: Performs a division on the given arguments - dividend and divisor.

functions.name: rodCoordSnap
functions.description: Snaps a rodCoord object so that its value is on the grid.

functions.name: rodCoordToFloat
functions.description: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as floating point number.

functions.name: rodCoordToInt
functions.description: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as a fixed number.

functions.name: rodCoordToString
functions.description: Returns a string containing the rodCoord data in user unit as floating number.

functions.name: rodCreateHandle
functions.signature: rodCreateHandle([ ?name S_name ][ ?type S_type ][ ?value g_value ][ ?rodObj R_rodObj ]);end rodCreateHandle=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a user-defined handle for any ROD object (named shape, instance, or cellview); the object must be at level zero in the hierarchy. For example, you can create a handle for polyRect or for instance I1, but not for I1/polyRect.

functions.description: Creates a path consisting of one or more parts at level zero in the hierarchy on the same or on different layers from a list of points or from one or more existing objects. A path consisting of multiple parts is called a multipart path. You can use the rodCreatePath function to create one-part paths, simple multipart paths, or complex multipart paths such as guard rings, transistors, buses, and shielded paths. You can assign one or more property names and values to a multipart path.

functions.name: rodCreatePolygon
functions.signature: rodCreatePolygon([ ?name S_name ][ ?layer txl_layer ][ ?pts l_pts ][ ?cvId d_cvId ][ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ][ ?size txf_size ][ ?prop l_prop ]; ROD Connectivity Arguments for Polygons[ ?netName S_netName ][ ?termName S_termName ][ ?termIOType S_termIOType ][ ?pin g_pin ][ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ][ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ][ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ][ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ][ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ][ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ][ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ][ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ][ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ][ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ]);end rodCreatePolygon=> R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Creates one polygon from a list of points or from one or more named objects. Also creates a ROD object containing information associated with the polygon, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. The polygon is created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the polygon. You can specify connectivity for the polygon by associating it with a specific terminal and net. You can also make the polygon into a pin.

functions.description: Creates a single named rectangle, one or more rows and/or columns of named rectangles, or fills a bounding box with named rectangles, where each rectangle has ROD attributes. You can create these named rectangles with the arguments S_name through g_returnBoolean. Each named rectangle is a separate object, created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can also create multipart rectangles by specifying one or more arrays of unnamed subrectangles for each named rectangle, where each unnamed subrectangle is an ordinary database shape, with no ROD attributes, created at level zero in the hierarchy. The named rectangles in a multipart rectangle are referred to as master rectangles.

functions.name: rodDeleteHandle
functions.description: Deletes a user-defined handle. You provide the ROD object ID and handle name.

functions.name: rodDeleteSubPart
functions.description: Deletes the named subpart from the given multipart path (MPP).

functions.name: rodFillBBoxWithRects
functions.signature: rodFillBBoxWithRects([ ?cvId d_cvId ][ ?layer txl_layer ][ ?fillBBox l_fillBBox ][ ?width n_width ][ ?length n_length ][ ?gap S_gap ][ ?spaceX n_spaceX ][ ?spaceY n_spaceY ][ ?prop l_prop ][ ?returnBoolean g_returnBoolean ]);end rodFillBBoxWithRects=> d_dbId / t / nil
functions.description: Fills a bounding box with rectangles, as many as fit within the bounding box you specify. The rectangles are ordinary unnamed shapes, identified by database IDs; the rectangles have no ROD attributes. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the set of rectangles. The property or list of properties apply to every rectangle in the bounding box. You specify the return value of the function to be Boolean or a list of the database IDs for the rectangles. When you want to create a one- or two-dimensional array of rectangles, and the rectangles do not need to be ROD objects, use this function instead of rodCreateRect because regular database shapes require less overhead, contributing to faster performance.

functions.name: rodFillWithRects
functions.signature: rodFillWithRects([ ?shapeId d_shapeID ][ ?fillShapeLPP lpp ][ ?fillShapeWidth n_width ][ ?fillShapeLength n_length ][ ?gap S_gap ][ ?justification S_justification ][ ?keepOut l_ptList ][ ?spaceX n_spaceX ][ ?spaceY n_spaceY ][ ?enclosureX n_encX ][ ?enclosureY n_encY ][ ?grid n_grid ][ ?outputFillShape l_dbId ]);end rodFillWithRects=> t / nil
functions.description: Fills a base shape with rectangles. The base shape can be a rectangle, polygon or a path type.

functions.name: rodForceUpdate
functions.description: Applies all ROD update requests in the queue.

functions.name: rodGetBBox
functions.signature: rodGetBBox([ ?figId d_figId ][ ?layer t_layer ][ ?purpose t_purpose ][ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ][ ?filterText g_filterText ]);end rodGetBBox=> l_bBox / nil
functions.description: Returns the coordinates of the rectangular bounding box enclosing all the elements of a specified figure on a specified layer. You can optionally limit the calculation to include only elements on a specified layer purpose and down to a specified level of design hierarchy. You can also exclude labels and text displays from the calculation.

functions.name: rodGetHandle
functions.description: Returns the value of a system- or user-defined handle. You specify the handle name and the ROD object ID for the object with which the handle is associated.

functions.name: rodGetNamedShapes
functions.description: Returns a list of the ROD object IDs for all named shapes (rectangles, polygons, and paths) at level zero in the hierarchy within the specified cellview that are ROD objects. This function looks only at the top level of hierarchy and does not return the ROD object ID for instances or cellviews.

functions.name: rodGetObj
functions.signature: rodGetObj(S_hierarchicalName | d_dbId[d_cellViewId]); end rodGetObj=> R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Lets you find a named object at any level of hierarchy in your cellview. You must specify either the database ID for the object or its hierarchical name. If you specify the hierarchical name, you must also specify the cellview ID. When you specify a cellview ID, it is not necessary to also specify the database ID; however, if you specify both, the cellview ID must be correct for the database ID you specify. If your rodGetObj statement occurs in the code for a Pcell (in the body of a pcDefinePCell function or tcCreateCDSDeviceClass function call), specifying the cellview ID is optional; if you do not specify it, the cellview ID defaults to pcCellView or tcCellView, respectively.

functions.name: rodGetSubPart
functions.description: Returns the subpart ID corresponding to the specified subpart name for the multipart path (MPP) specified as rodObjectId.

functions.name: rodIsFigNameUnused
functions.description: Determines whether the name specified by S_name is a valid name and whether it is already assigned to a ROD object, instance, or mosaic in the cellview specified by d_cvId. A valid name cannot contain hierarchy (indicated by one or more slashes) and cannot be an empty string.

functions.name: rodIsHandle
functions.description: Determines whether the name specified for S_name identifies a valid system- or user-defined handle associated with the object specified by R_rodObj. Use this function prior to the rodGetHandle function when you want to verify that the handle exists before you try to access it.

functions.name: rodIsMasterChoppable
functions.description: Returns the value of the MPP master path choppability attribute.

functions.name: rodIsObj
functions.description: Determines whether the object specified for g_object identifies a valid ROD object. This function is useful for testing variables and parameters to see if they contain a ROD object ID.

functions.name: rodNameObject
functions.signature: rodNameObject ([ ?name S_name ][ ?shapeId d_shapeId ][ ?permitRename g_permitRename ]);end rodNameObject=> R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Once the object is named, it can identified by a ROD object ID. This is an alias to an existing public function, rodNameShape.

functions.name: rodNameShape
functions.signature: rodNameShape([ ?name S_name ][ ?shapeId d_shapeId ][ ?permitRename g_permitRename ]);end rodNameShape=> R_rodObj / nil
functions.description: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Creates (or updates) a ROD object containing information associated with the shape, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. Optionally, you can specify whether to rename an existing ROD object.

functions.name: rodPointX
functions.description: Returns the X coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

functions.name: rodPointY
functions.description: Returns the Y coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

functions.name: rodSetMasterChoppable
functions.description: Sets the choppability attribute of an MPP master path to the specified value.

functions.name: rodSubPoints
functions.description: Subtracts l_point2 from l_point1 and returns the resulting point as l_point.

functions.name: rodUnAlign
functions.description: When you specify only one ROD object ID, removes all alignments for the object specified. When you specify two ROD object IDs, removes only the alignment between the two objects.

functions.name: rodUnNameShape
functions.description: Removes the name from a named shape or list of named shapes. The ROD object ID for the shape and all user-defined handles associated with it are deleted. If the object is an instance, the instance keeps its name but all user-defined handles associated with the instance are deleted. Also removes all alignment constraints that reference the shape.

functions.name: root
functions.description: Returns the nth X value at which the Y value equals the specified Y value (rootVal).

functions.name: rotatef
functions.description: Modifies the value of each place by rotating the values from one place to another in a cyclic order.

functions.name: round
functions.description: Rounds a floating-point number to its closest integer value.

functions.name: round2
functions.description: This function is a version of the round function that rounds the result in floating-point calculations to its closest integer value.

functions.name: rplaca
functions.description: Replaces the first element of a list with an object. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list, in the same way as setcar. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

functions.name: rplacd
functions.description: Replaces the tail of a list with the elements of a second list. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list in the same way as setcdr. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the changes.

functions.name: rshift
functions.description: Shifts the waveform to the right by the n_delta value.

functions.name: rteCheckAntenna
functions.signature: rteCheckAntenna([ ?cv d_cvid ][ ?all g_all ][ ?nets l_nets ][ ?set g_set ][ ?excludeNets l_excludeNets ][ ?model l_models ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Checks for process antenna violations for the entire design, specific nets, or nets in a set. You can choose to ignore specific nets.

functions.name: rteCheckDataForRouting
functions.signature: rteCheckDataForRouting([ ?mode t_mode ][ ?designRuleSpec t_designRuleSpec ][ ?fromRoutingLayer t_fromRoutingLayer ][ ?toRoutingLayer t_toRoutingLayer ][ ?annotate g_annotate ][ ?reportFileName t_reportFileName ][ ?selected g_selected ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Checks the technology data and the design data to ensure that the VSR router is able to perform correctly.

functions.name: rteCheckRoutability
functions.signature: rteCheckRoutability([ ?cv d_cvId ][ ?noBlockageCheck g_noBlockageCheck ][ ?noMinSpaceCheck g_noMinSpaceCheck ][ ?noMinWidthCheck g_noMinWidthCheck ][ ?noViaCheck g_noViaCheck ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Checks the design for known conditions that can cause potential routing problems. Design Rule Checks applied to pins and some routability checks are performed primarily to determine the accessibility of pins. You can exclude any of the checks by specifying the appropriate argument. Annotations are automatically created for violations.

functions.name: rteComposeTrunks
functions.description: Converts pathSegs and vias to power trunks usable by both the power and signal routers. The function uses the current cellview and the selected set.

functions.name: rteCoverObstructionHilite
functions.description: Turns on the cover obstruction hilite sets if at least one cover obstruction has been defined in the top-level or masters.

functions.name: rteCoverObstructionUnHilite
functions.description: Turns off the cover obstruction hilite sets for the ones that are already turned on, if at least one cover obstruction has been defined in the top-level or masters.

functions.name: rteCreateBlockRingScheme
functions.signature: rteCreateBlockRingScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?contour g_contour ][ ?channel g_channel ][ ?blockClearance f_blockClearance ][ ?horiLayer t_horiLayer ][ ?vertLayer t_vertLayer ][ ?latticeStyle g_latticeStyle ][ ?netClearance f_netClearance ][ ?netWidth f_netWidth ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a block ring routing scheme.

functions.name: rteCreateCellRowsScheme
functions.signature: rteCreateCellRowsScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?allRouteLayers g_allRouteLayers ][ ?routeLayers l_routeLayers ][ ?endOfRow g_endOfRow ][ ?extendToNearest g_extendToNearest ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a cell rows routing scheme.

functions.name: rteCreateCoreRingScheme
functions.signature: rteCreateCoreRingScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?ringAtCenter g_ringAtCenter ][ ?relativeTo s_relativeTo ][ ?coreClearance f_coreClearance ][ ?padClearance f_padClearance ][ ?inAreaClearance f_inAreaClearance ][ ?outAreaClearance f_outAreaClearance ][ ?areaXLo f_areaXLo ][ ?areaYLo f_areaYLo ][ ?areaXHi f_areaXHi ][ ?areaYHi f_areaYHi ][ ?horiLayer t_horiLayer ][ ?vertLayer t_vertLayer ][ ?latticeStyle g_latticeStyle ][ ?netClearance f_netClearance ][ ?netWidth f_netWidth ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a core ring routing scheme.

functions.name: rteCreatePadRingScheme
functions.signature: rteCreatePadRingScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?allPinLayers g_allPinLayers ][ ?pinLayers l_pinLayers ][ ?railPins g_railPins ][ ?edgePins g_edgePins ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a pad ring routing scheme.

functions.name: rteCreatePinToTrunkScheme
functions.signature: rteCreatePinToTrunkScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?allPinLayers g_allPinLayers ][ ?pinLayers l_pinLayers ][ ?useTrunkLayer g_useTrunkLayer ][ ?trunkLayer t_trunkLayer ][ ?minTrunkWidth f_minTrunkWidth ][ ?minWireWidth f_minWireWidth ][ ?maxWireWidth f_maxWireWidth ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a pin to trunk routing scheme. A trunk is usually a power net created by power routing commands such as pad ring, core ring, block ring, stripes, or cell rows.

functions.name: rteCreateStripesScheme
functions.signature: rteCreateStripesScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?horiStripes g_horiStripes ][ ?yStep f_yStep ][ ?horiLayers l_horiLayers ][ ?vertStripes g_vertStripes ][ ?xStep f_sStep ][ ?vertLayers l_vertLayers ][ ?pinClearance f_pinClearance ][ ?netClearance f_netClearance ][ ?netWidth f_netWidth ][ ?minStripeWidth f_minStripeWidth ][ ?offsetFrom s_offsetFrom ][ ?leftOffset f_leftOffset ][ ?bottomOffset f_bottomOffset ][ ?useCenterLine g_useCenterLine ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a stripes routing scheme.

functions.name: rteCreateViasScheme
functions.signature: rteCreateViasScheme([ ?name s_name ][ ?layerRange g_layerRange ][ ?minLayer t_minLayer ][ ?maxLayer t_maxLayer ][ ?cutArrayRule s_cutArrayRule ][ ?cutArrayRows n_cutArrayRows ][ ?cutArrayColumns n_cutArrayColumns ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a via insertion scheme.

functions.name: rteDecomposeTrunks
functions.description: Converts pathSegs and vias in power trunks to normal, routed pathSegs and vias. The function uses the current cellview and the selected set.

functions.name: rteDeleteRoutedNets
functions.description: Deletes the routed paths of all nets in the design. Optionally, you can preserve routed power nets.

functions.name: rteFixAntenna
functions.signature: rteFixAntenna([ ?cv d_cvid ][ ?all g_all ][ ?nets l_nets ][ ?set g_set ][ ?excludeNets l_excludeNets ][ ?layerList l_layerList ][ ?fullRulesChecking g_fullRulesChecking ][ ?maxWiresToPush x_maxWiresToPush ][ ?model l_models ][ ?useDiodes g_useDiodes ][ ?useJumpers g_useJumpers ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Fixes process antenna violations for the entire design, a specific net, or nets in a set by inserting jumpers and/or diodes. You can choose to ignore specific nets.

functions.name: rteFixViolations
functions.signature: rteFixViolations([ ?cv d_cvID ][ ?closeOpens g_closeOpens ][ ?excludeNet t_excludeNet ][ ?excludePowerGround g_excludePowerGround ][ ?fixCrossing g_fixCrossing ][ ?fixMfgGrid g_fixMfgGrid ][ ?fixMinArea g_fixMinArea ][ ?fixMinAreaAtPins g_fixMinAreaAtPins ][ ?fixMinEdge g_fixMinEdge ][ ?fixMinEncArea g_fixMinEncArea ][ ?fixMinWidth g_fixMinWidth ][ ?fixNumCuts g_fixNumCuts ][ ?fixPortShort g_fixPortShort ][ ?fixRouteGrid g_fixRouteGrid ][ ?reducePinWireNotches g_ReducePinWireNotches ][ ?maximizeCuts g_maximizeCuts ][ ?offsetVia g_offsetVia ][ ?region l_region ][ ?searchAndRepair g_searchAndRepair ][ ?set g_set ]s_value) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: This function allows you to fix violations for a selected area or for an entire cellview.

functions.name: rteGeomAnd
functions.signature: rteGeomAnd([ ?cv d_cvId ][ ?lpp1 g_lpp1 ][ ?lpp2 g_lpp2 ][ ?outputLpp l_outputLpp ][ ?blockedLayer l_blockedLayer ][ ?polygons g_polygons ][ ?region l_region ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Generates new shapes that are common on two or more layer purposes.

functions.name: rteGeomAndNot
functions.signature: rteGeomAndNot([ ?cv d_cvId ][ ?lpp1 g_lpp1 ][ ?lpp2 g_lpp2 ][ ?outputLpp l_outputLpp ][ ?blockedLayer l_blockedLayer ][ ?polygons g_polygons ][ ?region l_region ][ ?size1 f_size1 ][ ?size2 f_size2 ][ ?trimCorners g_trimCorners ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Generates new shapes that exist on one layer purpose and do not overlap shapes on another layer purpose. You can optionally use sized shapes from one or both of the layer purposes. And you can choose to operate on a specific region or the entire design.

functions.name: rteGeomNot
functions.signature: rteGeomNot([ ?cv d_cvId ][ ?lpp1 g_lpp1 ][ ?outputLpp l_outputLpp ][ ?blockedLayer l_blockedLayer ][ ?polygons g_polygons ][ ?region l_region ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Inverts the shapes on a layer purpose to generate new shapes.
