functions.signature: rteSearchAndRepair([ ?cv d_cvid ][ ?closeOpens g_closeOpens ][ ?excludeNet t_excludeNet ][ ?excludeType t_excludeType ][ ?set g_set ][ ?region l_region ][ ?fullRulesChecking g_fullRulesChecking ]) ;=> t / nil
functions.description: Searches for and fixes same net and different net spacing violations.

functions.name: run
functions.description: Starts the simulation or specifies a time after which an analysis should start. If distributed processing is not available on the system or is not enabled, the arguments specific to distributed processing (see Arguments section below for list of arguments specific to distributed processing) are ignored and the simulation runs locally. If distributed processing is available and is enabled, the environment default values are used if not specified in the run command arguments. The environmental default values are stored in the .cdsenv file.

functions.name: runsim
functions.description: Runs the SKILL instructions stored in the simCommand variable, which is used to run the simulator for this simulation. The function then calls simOutWithArgs with the correct arguments to translate the textual simulator output stored in the simout.tmp file and generate the si.out file.

functions.name: s11
functions.description: Returns s11 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S11 means the response at port1 due to a signal at port 1.

functions.name: s12
functions.description: Returns s12 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S12 means the response at port1 due to a signal at port 2.

functions.name: s21
functions.description: Returns s21 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S21 means the response at port 2 due to a signal at port 1.

functions.name: s22
functions.description: Returns s22 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S22 means the response at port 2 due to a signal at port 2.

functions.name: sample
functions.description: Samples a waveform at the specified interval.

functions.name: save
functions.signature: save([ ?categ s_categ ] s_saveType[ t_saveName1 ] ... [ t_saveNameN ])=> undefined / nil
functions.description: Specifies the outputs to be saved and printed during simulation.

functions.name: saveContext
functions.description: Saves the current state of the SKILL language interpreter as a binary file. This function must be used in conjunction with setContext.

functions.name: saveFloat
functions.description: Serializes the given floating point number (f_number) to string (t_string).

functions.name: saveGraphImage
functions.signature: saveGraphImage([ ?window x_window ][ ?fileName x_fileName ][ ?exactCopy g_exactCopy ][ ?quality x_quality ][ ?msOptimize g_msOptimize ][ ?width x_width ][ ?height x_height ][ ?units s_units ][ ?resolution x_resolution ][ ?resolutionUnits s_resolutionUnits ][ ?aspectRatio g_aspectRatio ][ ?enableTitle g_enableTitle ][ ?enableLegend g_enableLegend ][ ?enableAxes g_enableAxes ][ ?enableGrids g_enableGrids ][ ?backgroundColor s_backgroundColor ][ ?saveAllSubwindows g_saveAllSubwindows ][ ?saveEachSubwindowSeparately g_saveEachSubwindowSeparately ])=> x_fileName / nil
functions.description: Saves the graph as an image.

functions.name: saveOpPoint
functions.description: Specifies the operating point parameters to be saved for a given instance.

functions.name: saveOption
functions.signature: saveOption([ s_option1 g_optionValue1 ]...[ s_optionN g_optionValueN ])=> undefined / nil
functions.description: Specifies save options to be used by the simulator.

functions.name: saveSubckt
functions.signature: saveSubckt(t_name[ ?voltage g_voltage ][ ?current g_current ][ ?power g_power ][ ?vDepth s_vDepth ][ ?iDepth s_iDepth ][ ?pwrDepth s_pwrDepth ][ ?compress g_compress ][ ?filterRC g_filterRC ][ ?ports g_ports ][ ?userOptions g_userOptions ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Saves and modifies the specified subcircuit instances and signals.

functions.name: schAddIgnoreProp
functions.description: Registers an ignore property. You can view the set of registered ignore properties on the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor in the schematic window.

functions.name: schAddSelectPt
functions.description: Selects the object under the cursor. Maintains the selected set and adds the object to the selected set. Usable when editing schematics. Is equivalent to the Graphics Editor mouseAddSelectPt function. Provides other functions with the identity of the most recently selected object, which is required for extended selection.

functions.name: schAlign
functions.description: Aligns the objects in the specified direction in the schematic or symbol view.

functions.name: schAttachLibToPackageTech
functions.description: Attaches a package technology to the given library.

functions.name: schCheck
functions.description: Performs a check on the specified cellview. This includes extracting connectivity, running the schematic rules checker, and running the cross-view checker. You must have write permission to any cellview that is to be checked. The given cellview ID can be read-only or editable schematic.

functions.name: schCheckHier
functions.description: Performs a check of the hierarchy that starts at the given cellview.

functions.name: schCheckHierConfig
functions.description: Performs a check of the hierarchy. The check starts with the top cellview that is specified in the given hierarchy configuration. The hierarchy traversed is defined by information in this hierarchy configuration. Usually, the hierarchy is confined to the library of the given cellview, but you can specify a list of reference libraries to process if the hierarchy extends beyond the current library.

functions.name: schClearConn
functions.description: Removes the schematic connectivity from a specified cellview to restart extraction using schExtractConn.

functions.name: schCloneSymbol
functions.description: Copies or clones graphics from an existing symbol into the target symbol cellview with the given location and orientation.

functions.name: schCmdOption
functions.description: Cycles through a predefined set of values. By default, this function is bound to the middle mouse button. When you click the right mouse button during an active command, the command applies the next value in the predefined set.

functions.name: schComputePinRef
functions.signature: schComputePinRef(d_cellView[ ?reportFile t_reportFile ][ ?display t_display ][ ?formatString t_formatString ][ ?reportDups t_reportDups ][ ?sortByDir t_sortByDir ][ ?separator t_separator ][ ?inputDesignator t_inputDesignator ][ ?outputDesignator t_outputDesignator ][ ?ioDesignator t_ioDesignator ][ ?charsPerLine x_charsPerLine ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates offsheet pin references for multisheet designs. The pin references can be displayed in the schematic next to each pin or in a report file. This function creates an offsheet pin reference report that lists each pin followed by a list of all other locations of this pin. The pin references can also be displayed in the schematic next to each pin.

functions.name: schCopy
functions.description: Copies the given object to the given destination cellview. The object location and orientation can be specified before it is placed at the destination location by the given transformation argument. The copied figure is first rotated and reflected about the origin as specified by the orientation of the transform, then translated by the offset of the transform.

functions.name: schCreateInst
functions.description: Creates an instance of the given master cellview in the specified cellview at the given location with the given orientation. You can specify the magnification to set for the instance. Although not fully supported, you can use this property to scale the appearance of an instance.

functions.name: schCreateInstBox
functions.description: Creates an instance box in the given symbol cellview. This function uses a bounding box you specify or determines a bounding box from the pins and device shapes.

functions.name: schCreateNetExpression
functions.description: Creates an inherited connection and the corresponding net expression label. Attaches the given net expression to the given database object. It validates the syntax of the expression and attaches a net expression label to the database object. If the object is a schematic wire, you must run the schematic extractor to create the inherited connection. Before calling this function, you must acquire all the required arguments of the function.

functions.name: schCreateNoteLabel
functions.description: Creates note labels in a schematic or symbol cellview with the attributes and properties you specify. These labels do not affect the connectivity but can be useful for annotation.

functions.name: schCreateNoteShape
functions.description: Creates note shapes in a schematic or symbol cellview with the attributes and properties you specify. These shapes do not affect the connectivity but can be useful for annotation.

functions.name: schCreatePin
functions.description: Creates instances that are used to represent pins of terminals in a schematic cellview. Creates only a pin in a schematic cellview. The destination cellview must not be the same as the master cellview and must be editable.

functions.name: schCreateSheet
functions.description: Creates a new sheet for a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schCreateSplitPrimarySymbol
functions.description: Searches for split symbol views within the given cell and creates a split-primary symbol by assembling all the terminals from the gathered views. The generated split-primary cellview has the view name as symbol. This function removes an existing split-primary cellview, if any, and replaces it with a new one.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolLabel
functions.description: Creates a label in only a symbol cellview with the specified attributes that is opened in append mode.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolPin
functions.description: Creates a pin in the given cellview with the name, direction, and orientation you specify.

functions.name: schCreateSymbolShape
functions.description: Creates the specified shape using the given fill style and the list of points in the given cellview.

functions.name: schCreateWire
functions.description: Creates flight lines, wide wires, or narrow wires in the specified schematic cellview.

functions.name: schCreateWireLabel
functions.description: Creates wire labels and glues them to the object you specify.

functions.name: schDelete
functions.description: Deletes the figure or object you specify only from schematic or symbol cellviews.

functions.name: schDeleteIndex
functions.description: Deletes an index schematic if there is one remaining sheet. Converts the remaining sheet into an ordinary schematic with the cell name of the index schematic and replaces any offsheet pins with schematic pins.

functions.name: schDeleteSheet
functions.description: Deletes a sheet from a multisheet schematic design.

functions.name: schDeselectAllFig
functions.description: Deselects all objects in a specified cellview. Bypasses the selection filter.

functions.name: schDirectEdit
functions.description: Directly edits or manipulates the object under the cursor. Usable when editing schematics and symbols.

functions.name: schDistribute
functions.description: Arranges objects at equal distance in the specified direction in the schematic or symbol view.

functions.name: schDrawSymbolPin
functions.description: Creates a symbol pin in the specified cellview by creating a terminal of the given name with the given direction and a polygon shape specified by the given list of points.

functions.name: schEditPinOrder
functions.description: Updates the pin ordering for schematic or symbol cellviews given a list of pin names contained in the cellview and their desired order.

functions.name: schEditSheetSize
functions.description: Places or replaces a sheet border instance in a schematic. This function works for both multisheet and non-multisheet schematics.

functions.name: schExportSVG
functions.signature: schExportSVG(d_cellview?path s_path?background s_background?grid s_grid?stipple s_stipple?drawBBox g_drawBBox?nameCallback g_nameCallback)=> t / nil
functions.description: Exports a schematic as a vector image in SVG format.

functions.name: schExtendSelSet
functions.description: Extends the selection of the object in the specified position by selecting the object around the current object.

functions.name: schExtendSelectPt
functions.description: Extends the selection of the object under the current cursor position by selecting objects around the current object. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schExtractConn
functions.description: Runs the schematic connectivity extractor on the cellview you specify.

functions.name: schExtractStatus
functions.description: Checks for error and warning markers before returning the schematic extraction status for the specified schematic cellview. When the schematic is read-only, schExtractStatus() will also check whether any instance masters have been updated since the schematic was last saved.

functions.name: schFindIgnorePropByName
functions.description: Searches for an ignore property in the registered property set. You can view the registered ignore property set by clicking Options - Editor - Ignore Properties tab in the schematic window.

functions.name: schGetAllIgnoreProps
functions.description: Returns a disembodied property list for all the ignore properties that are currently registered. You can view the set of registered ignore properties set on the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor in the schematic window.

functions.name: schGetBundleDisplayMode
functions.description: Takes a label Id and returns its display mode. This only works for label type objects. If the specified object Id is not a label object, then the API will return nil. This will only work when the cellview is editable.

functions.name: schGetCellViewListInSearchScope
functions.description: Returns a list of cellviews in the search scope you specify. Only cellviews of the same view type as the base cellview are returned.

functions.name: schGetCheckGroups
functions.description: Returns an association list of all the custom schematic checker groups created using schRegisterCheckGroup().

functions.name: schGetEnv
functions.description: Gets the value of a schematic environment variable.

functions.name: schGetIgnoredStatus
functions.description: Returns the ignored status of the given instance ID. This function can be used only when the instance IDs are known.

functions.name: schGetMatchingObjects
functions.description: Finds the set of objects that match the specified search criteria in a cellview. You can search by property to limit the search in the selected set.

functions.name: schGetPinOrder
functions.description: Returns the pin list, as defined in the portOrder property (if present) or as the default pin list.

functions.name: schGetPostCheckTriggers
functions.description: Lists all the post-check triggers registered using schRegPostCheckTrigger.

functions.name: schGetPreCheckTriggers
functions.description: Lists all the pre-check triggers registered using schRegPreCheckTrigger.

functions.name: schGetPropertyDisplay
functions.signature: schGetPropertyDisplay(?object d_object[?name S_name])=> l_textDisplays / s_visibility / nil
functions.description: Returns the attribute, property, and parameter textDisplays enabled for an object.

functions.name: schGetShapeStyle
functions.description: Returns a Disembodied property list (DPL) containing the style attributes of a given shape.

functions.name: schGetSignalTypeIntegrity
functions.description: Gets the conflict severity for signal type integrity check for connections between nets of specified signal type, and instance pins of specified signal type and direction.

functions.name: schGetSplitInstTerms
functions.description: Returns a list of split instance terminals that have the same name as that of the given split-primary instance.

functions.name: schGetSplitInstances
functions.description: Returns a list of split instance IDs that are associated with the given split-primary instance.

functions.name: schGetSplitPrimaryInst
functions.description: Returns the split-primary instance associated with the given split symbol.

functions.name: schGetSplitPrimaryInstTerm
functions.description: Returns the terminal of the split-primary instance that has the same terminal name as the specified split instance terminal.

functions.name: schGetWireColor
functions.description: Returns the color used to draw a wire segment.

functions.name: schGetWireLineStyle
functions.description: Returns the line style used to draw a wire segment.

functions.name: schGlueLabel
functions.description: Glues the label to the figure you specify using a database child/parent relationship in which the label is the child. You can glue a pin label to a pin only when the label defines the name for that pin. You can glue a wire label only to a wire, a pin of a component, or a pin of a schematic. The label defines the name of the net associated with the wire, the pin of the component, or the pin of the schematic. You can glue note labels to any object.

functions.name: schHDLReturn
functions.description: Returns up the hierarchy from a Verilog view window.

functions.name: schHdlPrintFile
functions.description: Prints the current HDL file.

functions.name: schHdlPrintVars
functions.description: Prints the current values of the schematic HDL variables.

functions.name: schHiAbout
functions.description: Opens the product information window, which indicates the schematic editor release number and copyright information.

functions.name: schHiAlign
functions.description: Aligns the objects on the canvas. If the objects are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for aligning the objects.

functions.name: schHiAlternateView
functions.description: Changes the view name of a single component by toggling through the list of possible views. Usable only while editing a schematic cellview. Operates on one instance at a time.

functions.name: schHiCellViewProperty
functions.description: Displays the options form showing the properties for the current cellview. Usable only when editing schematic or symbol cellviews.

functions.name: schHiChangeEditMode
functions.description: Sets the mode for the design in the current window to read or append. The mode is the same as that supplied to dbOpenCellViewByType.

functions.name: schHiCheck
functions.description: Checks the connectivity of a schematic and optionally starts the schematic rules checker (SRC) or the cross-view checker (VIC). Usable only when editing schematics. A dialog box shows the total number of errors and warnings detected when the function is complete. The schematic can be read-only or editable.

functions.name: schHiCheckAndSave
functions.description: Performs the checks specified by the check options and saves the schematic to disk under the same cell name and view name, and in the same library. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCheckHier
functions.description: Performs the specified checks on the current schematic and the hierarchy below it. Also updates the connectivity as needed and runs the schematic rules checker (SRC), the cross-view checker (VIC), or both. Usable only when editing schematics. Only processes schematics found in the hierarchy starting from the current cellview. The view name list used to control the traversal is taken from the window in which the function is run.

functions.name: schHiCloneSymbol
functions.description: Copies graphics from an existing symbol library into the symbol design you are currently editing. Usable only when editing symbols. If you do not specify any argument, the options form appears and prompts you for the values of these fields.

functions.name: schHiComputePinRef
functions.signature: schHiComputePinRef([ ?reportFile t_reportFile ][ ?display t_display ][ ?formatString t_formatString ][ ?reportDups t_reportDups ][ ?sortByDir t_sortByDir ])=> t
functions.description: Displays the Cross-Reference Options form for current index or sheet schematic, which computes, stores, and lists zone references for all pins and offsheet connectors in a multisheet schematic. The zone references identify where pins on other sheets reference the same net. Uses stored references to identify pin locations. The pin references can be displayed in the schematic alongside each pin or written to a report file. Can be used only when editing either the index or a sheet of a multisheet design. The index requires checking before zones can be computed.

functions.name: schHiCopy
functions.signature: schHiCopy([ ?formFlag g_formFlag ][ ?rows x_numrows ][ ?columns x_numcols ][ ?useSelSet t_useSelSet ])=> t
functions.description: Copies objects and data such as object properties. Objects can be copied between different schematic cellviews. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateBlockInst
functions.signature: schHiCreateBlockInst([ ?libraryName t_libraryName ][ ?cellName t_cellName ][ ?viewName t_viewName ][ ?blockSampleName t_blockSampleName ][ ?instanceName t_instanceName ][ ?pinNameSeed t_pinNameSeed ])=> t
functions.description: Creates a block and places an instance of a block in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics. If you do not type a library, cell, view, and instance name as arguments, the options form appears and prompts you for these values. The block choices are defined by the schBlockTemplate variable in the schConfig.il file. If you type freeform, the schematic editor prompts you to type a rectangular shape by clicking on two points of the rectangle.

functions.name: schHiCreateInst
functions.signature: schHiCreateInst([ ?libraryName t_libraryName ][ ?cellName t_cellName ][ ?viewName t_viewName ][ ?instanceName t_instanceName ][ ?rows x_rows ][ ?columns x_columns ])=> t
functions.description: Places an instance of a cellview in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateInstBox
functions.description: Creates an instance box for the symbol you are editing. An instance box defines a rectangular region in which an instance of a symbol is selectable. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateKanjiSymbol
functions.signature: schHiCreateKanjiSymbol([ ?kanjiFile t_kanjiFile ][ ?libName t_libName ][ ?cellName t_cellName ][ ?viewName t_viewName ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Creates a symbol view containing kanji characters based on the information in an EUC-packed format kanji file. The software generates a symbol cellview that contains kanji character graphics.

functions.name: schHiCreateMappingSchematic
functions.description: Displays the Create a Mapping Schematic form.

functions.name: schHiCreateNetExpression
functions.signature: schHiCreateNetExpression([ ?netExpr t_netExpr ][ ?justify t_justify ][ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ][ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ])=> t
functions.description: Creates an inherited connection and the corresponding net expression label. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateNoteLabel
functions.signature: schHiCreateNoteLabel([ ?text t_text ][ ?justify t_justify ][ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ][ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ][ ?type t_type ])=> t
functions.description: Creates a note label to annotate the design for documentation purposes. These shapes do not affect connectivity. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateNoteShape
functions.description: Creates a shape to annotate the design for documentation purposes. These shapes do not affect connectivity. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreatePatchcord
functions.description: Displays the Create Patchcord form where you can create, and add, a patchCord instance on a schematic along with appropriately named net stubs.

functions.name: schHiCreatePin
functions.signature: schHiCreatePin([ ?terminalName t_terminalName ][ ?direction t_direction ][ ?usage t_usage ][ ?interpret t_interpret ][ ?mode t_mode ][ ?netExpr t_netExpr ][ t_justify ][ t_fontStyle ][ n_fontHeight ])=> t
functions.description: Creates a pin of a specified type in your schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateSheet
functions.description: Creates a sheet for a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolLabel
functions.signature: schHiCreateSymbolLabel([ ?labelChoice t_labelChoice ][ ?text t_text ][ ?justify t_justify ][ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ][ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ][ ?type t_type ])=> t
functions.description: Places labels in a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolPin
functions.signature: schHiCreateSymbolPin([ ?terminalName t_terminalName ][ ?type t_type ][ ?direction t_direction ][ ?interpret t_interpret ][ ?mode t_mode ][ ?incrCount n_incrCount ][ ?location t_location ])=> t
functions.description: Creates pins in a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateSymbolShape
functions.signature: schHiCreateSymbolShape([ ?shape t_shape ][ ?style t_style ][ ?width x_width ][ ?nonModal g_nonModal ])=> t
functions.description: Creates a line or shapes that describe a symbol. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiCreateWire
functions.signature: schHiCreateWire([ ?width n_width ][ ?drawMode g_drawMode ][ ?routeMethod t_routeMethod ][ ?lockAngle t_lockAngle ][ ?nonModal g_nonModal ][ ?color t_color ][ ?lineStyle t_lineStyle ])=> t
functions.description: Creates different style wires that represent net connections in a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateWireLabel
functions.signature: schHiCreateWireLabel([ ?text t_text ][ ?purpose t_purpose ][ ?justify t_justify ][ ?fontStyle t_fontStyle ][ ?fontHeight n_fontHeight ][ ?interpret t_interpret ][ ?mode t_mode ][ ?netExprFlag g_netExprFlag ][ ?bundleDisplay t_bundleDisplay ])=> t
functions.description: Creates wire labels in a schematic. Physical contact between a label and wire is not required. You can move a label independently from a wire. When you move a wire that has a label glued to it, the label also moves. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiCreateWireStubs
functions.description: Starts the Create Wire Stubs and Names command.

functions.name: schHiDefaultAction
functions.description: Performs the default editing action for the object under the cursor.

functions.name: schHiDelete
functions.description: Deletes selected objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. This function cannot be used to delete a sheet border (use schHiEditSheetSize).

functions.name: schHiDeleteIndex
functions.description: Converts a multisheet schematic having one drawing sheet and one index sheet into a single-sheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index schematic. Use schHiDeleteSheet to first remove extra drawing sheets. The index schematic must contain only one sheet.

functions.name: schHiDeleteSheet
functions.description: Deletes a sheet or range of sheets from a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index of a multisheet schematic. This function cannot be undone.

functions.name: schHiDescend
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview of a specified instance and view you select, provided you have edit permission. If you do not have edit permission, a dialog box prompts you to use read mode.

functions.name: schHiDescendEdit
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview of a specified instance and view you select, provided you have edit permission. If you do not have edit permission, a dialog box prompts you to use read mode.

functions.name: schHiDescendRead
functions.description: Traverses down the hierarchy and displays the child cellview in read mode of a specified instance and view you select. The cellview is not editable.

functions.name: schHiDisplayOptions
functions.description: Sets options associated with the window display. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiDistribute
functions.description: Arranges the objects on the canvas at equal distance from each other. If the objects are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for distributing the objects.

functions.name: schHiDrawSymbolPin
functions.description: Draws a polygon that represents a symbol pin. Usable only when editing symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditInPlace
functions.description: Edits the master of a user-selected instance within the context of its parent schematic. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditPinOrder
functions.description: Creates or modifies the property on the cellview that specifies the ordering of the pins in the current cellview. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEditSheetSize
functions.description: Edits the sheet border size of a schematic. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiEditText
functions.description: Starts the direct text edit command in the current window, allowing you to perform an in-place edit of notes, names, parameters, and so on.

functions.name: schHiEditTitleBlock
functions.description: Changes the properties of a title block in a schematic sheet. Usable only when editing schematics that have a sheet border.

functions.name: schHiEditorOptions
functions.description: Sets variables that affect the environment. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEnvSaveLoad
functions.description: Saves or loads the schematic environment variables. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiEscape
functions.description: Closes an open form or clears the current canvas selection. You would typically use this function to successively close the open forms on your desktop, even if they are hidden behind other windows. If there is only one form open, it is closed. If there are multiple forms open, the first form returned by the hiGetCurrentForm SKILL API is closed. If there are no forms open, the current canvas selection is cleared.

functions.name: schHiExtractConn
functions.description: Sets extraction options and runs the schematic extractor. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiFind
functions.description: Finds objects that match specified search criteria in a schematic or symbol view. You can specify the object filter as well as a property name or value expression that matches the objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. Matching is supported only for strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and time. Other property types are not supported.

functions.name: schHiFindMarker
functions.description: Searches for the error and warning markers generated by the schematic rules checker (SRC) and displays a form that contains a list of the markers. Usable when editing a schematic or a symbol.

functions.name: schHiFlatten
functions.description: Starts the schematic Flatten command. Flattening brings the contents of the flattened instance up to the current level to allow editing while preserving the connectivity of the flattened instance. If no single, valid instance is pre-selected, it prompts you to select an instance to flatten. When a valid instance is selected, it prompts you to select a point to place the flattened content. In the case of schematic-in-schematic, the flattened content is placed immediately, without prompting for an additional point.

functions.name: schHiFollowPin
functions.description: Changes the cellview to one that contains the specified pin or offsheet connector. Operates on the selected set. Brings in the cellview that contains the first reference of the selected pin or offsheet connector. Usable only when editing a sheet of a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schHiFontUpdate
functions.description: Interactive command for updating the font size of text on a schematic.

functions.name: schHiGotoSheet
functions.description: Traverses sheets in a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index or sheet of a multisheet schematic.

functions.name: schHiGridOptions
functions.description: Sets options associated with the grid.

functions.name: schHiHiliteLabel
functions.description: Highlights labels of wires and instances. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiIgnore
functions.description: Ignores the instances in the schematic canvas. This function works as a toggle switch, that is, it is used for adding ignore properties to an instance or for removing any existing ones. When the instances are already selected on the canvas, the pre-select mode is used; otherwise, the post-select mode is used for ignoring the instances.

functions.name: schHiInstToView
functions.description: Generates a cellview from an instance of a symbol. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiMakeCell
functions.description: Starts the schematic Make Cell command. Make Cell cuts out a rectangular region of the schematic, moving it into a new schematic cellview, and fills in the gap with a new hierarchical instance. The command adjusts the design hierarchy without changing the connectivity. You can define the rectangular area you wish to cut.

functions.name: schHiMousePopUp
functions.description: Displays a pop-up menu at the location of the cursor. The menu displayed is sensitive to the location of the cursor and the mode of the cellview in the window. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiMove
functions.description: Moves objects to a different location. You can move objects between different schematic and symbol cellviews. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. Partially selected objects cannot be moved to a different cellview. Does not support change in orientation for partially selected objects.

functions.name: schHiNetExprAvailProps
functions.description: Displays the Net Expression Available Property Names form. Use this form to find the net expression property names that are available for setting on the selected instances.

functions.name: schHiNetExprEvalNames
functions.description: Displays the Net Expression Evaluated Names form. Use this form to view the net names that result from the evaluation of all net expressions that are found in the hierarchy below the selected instances.

functions.name: schHiNewCellView
functions.description: Displays the Create New File form. This function needs to be invoked from a window that contains either schematic or symbol data.

functions.name: schHiObjectProperty
functions.description: Displays a form that lets you modify the properties of selected objects. Usable only when editing a schematic or symbol cellview.

functions.name: schHiOpenCellView
functions.description: Displays the Open File form. You specify the library name, cell name, view name, and edit mode in this form. The specified cellview is displayed in the current window. Usable for opening schematic and symbol design windows.

functions.name: schHiOpenOtherView
functions.signature: schHiOpenOtherView(d_cellViewID[ t_viewNames ][ w_windowID ][ w_sessionWindowID ])=> nil / windowID
functions.description: Allows you to switch between schematic and symbol views.

functions.name: schHiOpenSymbolOrSchematicView
functions.description: Takes the current viewtype, schematic or symbol, then calls schHiOpenOtherView to then switch between the views.

functions.name: schHiPinListToView
functions.signature: schHiPinListToView([ ?libName t_libName ][ ?cellName t_cellName ][ ?viewName t_viewName ][ ?inPinList t_inPinList ][ ?outPinList t_outPinList ][ ?ioPinList t_ioPinList ][ ?swPinList t_swPinList ][ ?dataType t_dataType ][ ?jpPinList t_jpPinList ][ ?trPinList t_trPinList ][ ?unPinList t_unPinList ])=> t
functions.description: Generates a cellview from a pin list. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiPlot
functions.description: Brings up the Submit Plot form to let you generate schematic plots. Usable when viewing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiPlotQueueStatus
functions.description: Displays the plot jobs in the spooling queues. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiRaiseCurrentForm
functions.description: Brings the most recently-used open form to the front. If there are no open forms, the command does nothing. Bound to F3 by default.

functions.name: schHiRegisterWireStubs
functions.description: Invokes the Register Net Name per Terminal form.

functions.name: schHiRenumberAllSheet
functions.description: Sequentially renumbers all sheets in a multisheet schematic. Usable only when editing an index schematic.

functions.name: schHiRenumberInstances
functions.description: Opens the Renumber Instances form which can be used to renumber instances automatically.

functions.name: schHiRenumberSheet
functions.description: Changes the number of a sheet in a multisheet schematic. Changes the cell name of the renumbered schematic to match the destination sheet number. If a sheet already exists with the destination number, the renumbered sheet is inserted before it. All succeeding sheets will be renumbered accordingly.

functions.name: schHiReplace
functions.signature: schHiReplace([ ?replaceAll g_replaceAll ][ ?propName t_propName ][ ?condOp t_condOp ][ ?propValue t_propValue ][ ?newPropName t_newPropName ][ ?newPropValue t_newPropValue ])=> t
functions.description: Replaces objects that match the specified search criteria with a specified value. Usable when editing symbols or schematics. You must have write access to each of the cellviews. Only supports matching of strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and time. This function does not support other property types.

functions.name: schHiResetInvisibleLabels
functions.description: Causes the highlighted labels to either remain visible or reverse to the invisible state in the design. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiReturn
functions.description: Returns up the hierarchy. Usable when editing schematics or symbols after completing a descend or edit-in-place action.

functions.name: schHiReturnToTop
functions.description: Returns to the top-level cellview in the hierarchy. Usable when editing schematics or symbols after completing a series of descend commands.

functions.name: schHiRotate
functions.description: Rotates objects. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiRouteFlightLine
functions.description: Routes logical connections shown as flight lines. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiRouteNamedConnection
functions.description: Starts an interactive command for converting existing wire-by-name connections into wired connections.

functions.name: schHiSRC
functions.description: Sets schematic rules checker (SRC) options, and runs the schematic rules checker. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiSaveCellView
functions.description: Saves the design in the current window.

functions.name: schHiSelectAll
functions.description: Opens a form that you use either to add all specified objects to the selected set or to delete all specified objects from the selected set. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiSelectByProperty
functions.signature: schHiSelectByProperty([ ?select t_select ][ ?propName t_propName ][ ?condOp t_condOp ][ ?propValue t_propValue ])=> t
functions.description: Adds objects that match specified search criteria in a schematic or symbol view to the selected set or removes objects that match specified search criteria in a schematic or symbol view from the selected set. Usable when editing schematics or symbols. Supports only selection of strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and time. This function does not support other property types.

functions.name: schHiSetOrigin
functions.description: Enables to change the origin point of a symbol or schematic. If you place the cell after specifying the origin point, it is automatically placed at the new origin point.

functions.name: schHiSetSymbolOrigin
functions.description: Relocates the origin point of a symbol and prompts you for a location of the new symbol origin point. All objects in the symbol are moved so when you later place the symbol, it is positioned on the dragging pointer relative to the new origin point.

functions.name: schHiShowScope
functions.description: Displays a dialog box describing the current hierarchical scope in the window. Usable when editing or reading schematics or symbols. The scope contains a list of instance names and the corresponding cell names.

functions.name: schHiSnapToGrid
functions.description: Places the objects on the grid in the given window. If the objects are already selected, the Snap To Grid command runs in the pre-select mode. If no object is selected in the given window, the command runs in the post-select mode.

functions.name: schHiSolder
functions.description: Creates a solder dot over a + or T wire segment. Usable only when editing schematics.

functions.name: schHiStretch
functions.description: Moves objects or partially selected objects and maintains connectivity with rubberband lines. Usable only when editing schematics. You cannot stretch objects between two different cellviews.

functions.name: schHiSymStretch
functions.description: Moves partially selected objects in the symbol editor. Can only be used when editing a symbol. Stretching between two different cellviews is not supported. When stretching an edge of a device border, the pin stubs attached to it are not dragged.

functions.name: schHiTree
functions.description: Used to display the design hierarchy listed in text format in the Tree Output window.

functions.name: schHiUpdatePinOrder
functions.description: Creates or modifies the property on the cellview that specifies the ordering of the pins in the current cellview. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiUpdatePinsFromView
functions.description: Updates the pin information in the current cellview from another view of the same cell. This works from schematic to symbol cellview, and vice-versa.

functions.name: schHiVHDLProperty
functions.description: Edits properties specific to the schematic and VHDL netlister. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiVIC
functions.description: Runs the cross-view checker (VIC) to check the consistency of the interface of one or more cellviews against the cellview you are editing. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schHiVICAndSave
functions.description: Runs the cross-view checker (VIC) on the cellview in the current active window and saves the cellview.

functions.name: schHiViewToView
functions.signature: schHiViewToView([ ?libName t_libName ][ ?cellName t_cellName ][ ?viewNameFrom t_viewNameFrom ][ ?viewNameTo t_viewNameTo ][ ?dataType t_dataType ])=> t
functions.description: Generates one type of cellview from another.

functions.name: schHiZoomToSelSet
functions.description: Zooms to selected objects in the current window. If no objects are selected prior to actioning the function, you will be prompted to draw a selection area.

functions.name: schIgnore
functions.description: Adds or removes the ignore properties from the specified instance. You can view the registered ignore properties on the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor.

functions.name: schInhConFind
functions.description: Given a windowId and an optional list of instances (or all instances in the window if none are explicitly specified), will return a list of inherited connections eligible for override beneath these instances.

functions.name: schInhConSet
functions.signature: schInhConSet(t_inhCon[ ?name t_name ][ ?default t_default ][ ?value t_value ][ ?pinName t_pinName ][ ?pinDir t_pinDir ][ ?pinPos t_pinPos ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Manipulates inherited connections located using schInhConFind.

functions.name: schInstToView
functions.description: Generates a cellview type from an instance of a symbol.

functions.name: schInstallHDL
functions.description: Installs a Verilog HDL source file as an HDL cellview and creates the cell, view, and cellview objects in the library if necessary. This function can also create a matching symbol cellview.

functions.name: schIsFlightLine
functions.description: Checks if the specified object is a flight line on a net.

functions.name: schIsHDLCapEnabled
functions.description: Validates that a license supporting the schematic editing feature is already checked out and does a recheck to ensure that the license has not timed out. Otherwise, attempts to check out a license.

functions.name: schIsInCheckHier
functions.description: Identifies and performs the specific actions, as mentioned in the SKILL code, when checking a design hierarchy as opposed to a single cellview during a schematic hierarchy check. When you check a design hierarchy or a single cellview, the schematic checker runs any pre or post check triggers and custom checker rules that you have previously registered.

functions.name: schIsIndexCV
functions.description: Tests whether the given cellview is an index schematic cellview.

functions.name: schIsSchEditOk
functions.description: Checks if the given cellview is a schematic view, whether it is writable, and also whether the edit capability (VSE license successfully checked out) is enabled.

functions.name: schIsSheetCV
functions.description: Tests whether the given cellview is a multisheet schematic cellview.

functions.name: schIsSplitInst
functions.description: Tests if a specified instance is a split instance. An instance is a split instance if its master is a split symbol.

functions.name: schIsSplitPrimaryInst
functions.description: Tests if a specified instance is a split-primary instance.

functions.name: schIsSplitPrimarySymbol
functions.description: Tests if a specified cellview is a split-primary symbol.

functions.name: schIsSplitSymbol
functions.description: Tests if a specified cellview is a split symbol.

functions.name: schIsSymEditOk
functions.description: Checks if the given cellview is a schematic symbol view, whether it is writable, and also whether the edit capability (VSE license successfully checked out) is enabled.

functions.name: schIsTextEditable
functions.description: Queries whether or not a label (optionally inside an instance) can be edited directly on the canvas.

functions.name: schIsUsingSplitFeature
functions.description: Indicates if a specified cellview uses the split feature. This implies that a schematic cellview has split instances with correctly set split-primary instances and a symbol cellivew is a split or has a split-primary symbol.

functions.name: schIsWire
functions.description: Checks if the specified object is a wire.

functions.name: schIsWireLabel
functions.description: Tests whether the given database figure is a schematic wire label.

functions.name: schLayoutToPinList
functions.description: Translates a layout cellview into an intermediate pin list format. The pin list represents all of the terminals in the layout and their directions. The pin list also represents the cellview level properties in the maskLayout.

functions.name: schMapMCCleanup
functions.description: Cleans up the migration running directory from the directories and files generated during migration. Additionally, it removes definitions and folders of temporary libraries.

functions.name: schMapMCCreateTargets
functions.description: Creates targets for routing after placing the missing devices in the target cellviews.

functions.name: schMapMCFinalizeTargets
functions.description: Finalizes the assembly of the target cells and libraries. This SKILL function is equivalent to the Finalize Multiple Target Schematics (Part 3) option. In CIW, this option is available in Tools - Migrate - Multiple Schematics Mapping.

functions.name: schMapMCSaveSourceData
functions.description: Prepares all the cells, which are defined in the cell list file for migration. This SKILL function is equivalent to the Save Multiple Source Schematics Data (Part 1) option. In CIW, this option is available in Tools - Migrate - Multiple Schematics Mapping.

functions.name: schMapMCSettings
functions.signature: schMapMCSettings ([?rundir x_rundir][?mcrundir x_inputdatadir][?tgtlibsdir x_targetlibsdir][?cellsfile x_cellfilename][?tgtprefix x_temptargetlibsprefix][?dfntgtlibsbn g_redefinetargetlibs])=> t
functions.description: Assigns values to the settings that are used to carry out the batch multicell schematic migration. This SKILL function is equivalent to the Multiple Schematics Mapping - Settings option. In CIW, this option is available in Tools - Migrate.

functions.name: schMouseApplyOrFinish
functions.description: Adds a point and applies or finishes the active enter function command based on the setting of the modalCommands schematic environment variable. It is designed to be used for double-clicking with the left mouse button.

functions.name: schMove
functions.description: Moves the object you specify to a destination cellview. The object location and orientation can be specified before the object is placed at the destination location by the given transformation argument. The copied figure is first rotated and reflected about the origin as specified by the orientation of the transform, then translated by the offset of the transform.

functions.name: schNetExprAvailProps
functions.description: Returns a list of available properties, and their evaluated values, for the various occurrences passed.

functions.name: schNetExprEvalNames
functions.description: Returns a list of evaluated names for all occurrences specified.

functions.name: schPinListToSchem
functions.description: Generates a schematic cellview from a pin list.

functions.name: schPinListToSchemGen
functions.description: Opens the Create Schematic form if t_viewName is a schematic.

functions.name: schPinListToSymbol
functions.description: Generates a symbol cellview from a pin list.

functions.name: schPinListToSymbolGen
functions.description: Generates a symbol cellview from a pin list.

functions.name: schPinListToVerilog
functions.description: Generates a Verilog HDL cellview from a pin list. The generated Verilog HDL cellview can be used with the Verilog integration.

functions.name: schPinListToView
functions.description: Generates a cellview from a pin list.

functions.name: schPlot
functions.description: Generates a plot. The plot is defined in the t_file plot template file. If you do not specify t_file, this function uses the plot options stored in the schPlotOptions property list. If you backannotate the schematic and you specify w_windowId, the generated plot has backannotated values.

functions.name: schProduceCVHierConfig
functions.description: Traverses a configuration design hierarchy and invokes a callback for each unique cellview.

functions.name: schProduceUniqueCVHier
functions.description: Traverses a design hierarchy and invokes a procedure callback for each unique cellview.

functions.name: schRegPostCheckTrigger
functions.description: Registers a function that will be called after a schematic is checked using the Check - Current Cellview or Check - Hierarchy commands. The called function must be defined to accept three arguments: the cellview ID of the schematic, the number of errors encountered, and the number of warnings encountered during the check.

functions.name: schRegPreCheckTrigger
functions.description: Registers a function that will be called before a schematic is checked using the Check - Current Cellview or Check - Hierarchy commands. The called function must be defined to accept one argument; that is the cellview ID of the schematic.

functions.name: schRegisterCheckGroup
functions.signature: schRegisterCheckGroup([ ?name s_name ][ ?title t_title ][ ?description t_description ][ ?enabled g_enabled ])=> r_checkgroup / nil
functions.description: Creates and registers a new custom schematic checker group. Each new group appears as a discrete tab in the Schematic Rules Checks Setup form. Calling the function with the same group name as an existing group overwrites that group and all its rules.

functions.name: schRegisterCheckRule
functions.signature: schRegisterCheckRule([ ?title t_title ][ ?name s_name ][ ?groupName s_groupName ][ ?checkCB u_checkCB ][ ?configCB u_customCB ][ ?severity s_severity ][ ?description t_description ])=> r_checkrule / nil
functions.description: Creates and registers a new schematic rule checker. Calling this function with the same rule name as an existing rule in the same group overwrites that rule.

functions.name: schRegisterFixedMenu
functions.description: Registers a vertical fixed-menu handle for specific cellview types to customize the schematic and symbol editor fixed menus. This function also registers triggers to enable and disable specific items in the fixed menu based on whether the editor window is in edit or read mode.

functions.name: schRegisterPopUpMenu
functions.description: Replaces the object-sensitive menus (OSMs) of the schematic canvas with a specific object category and edit mode. This function should only be called after a schematic cellview has been opened and the schematic editor has been initialized. To ensure this, call schRegisterPopUpMenu() from a callback registered using deRegUserTriggers().

functions.name: schReinitializeShapeStyles
functions.description: Updates the style of all schematic shapes in the current session to reflect any changes made in the Display Resource Editor. Use this function to refresh non-default shape styles, for example, custom wire line styles and colors.

functions.name: schRemoveIgnoreProp
functions.description: Removes the specified ignore property from the registered ignore property set. You can view the registered ignore properties in the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor.

functions.name: schRenumberAllSheet
functions.description: Resequences all sheets starting at 1 and fills any holes in the sequence.

functions.name: schRenumberInstances
functions.signature: schRenumberInstances(g_objId[ t_scope ][ g_verbose ][ t_sequence ][ x_startIndex ][ t_applyTo [ t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName ] ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Resequences instances using the format instNamePrefix number that results in unique numbering indexes for each component name prefix encountered. Any voids in a numbering sequence are resolved by renaming instances with the highest numbers to fill the voids.

functions.name: schRenumberSheet
functions.description: Changes the number of a sheet in a multisheet schematic and changes the cell name of the renumbered schematic to match the destination sheet number. If a sheet already exists with the destination number, the new sheet is inserted before it and all succeeding sheets are renumbered accordingly.

functions.name: schReplaceProperty
functions.description: Changes the value of t_propName to t_propValue for the object. This function checks if the net, pin terminal, and master properties exist for the object.

functions.name: schReportCheckFailure
functions.signature: schReportCheckFailure([ ?object d_object ][ ?checkRule r_checkRule ][ ?message t_message ][ ?short t_short ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Report the failure of a custom schematic check rule.

functions.name: schSRC
functions.description: Runs the schematic rules checker (SRC) on a specified cellview.

functions.name: schSaveCurrentPlotOptions
functions.description: Writes the current plot settings to a file.

functions.name: schSchemToPinList
functions.description: Generates a pin list from a schematic cellview.

functions.name: schSelectAllFig
functions.description: Selects all objects in a cellview that pass the selection filter.

functions.name: schSelectByLine
functions.description: Selects objects by drawing a path across the Virtuoso Schematic Editor window. The objects are highlighted based on what is specified in the Schematic Selection Filter form.

functions.name: schSelectPoint
functions.description: Interactively selects the object under the cursor. With single selection, this function first deselects all objects on the selected set. With additive selection, this function maintains the selected set and adds the current object to the selected set.

functions.name: schSetAndLoadTsgTemplateType
functions.description: Sets the tsgTemplateType environment variable and loads the corresponding tsg template file.

functions.name: schSetBundleDisplayMode
functions.description: Takes a label Id whose display mode is to be changed and applies either a vertical or horizontal display value. This will only work when the cellview is editable.

functions.name: schSetCmdOption
functions.description: Customizes which form fields are modified by calls to schCmdOption, middle mouse button, and schShiftCmdOption, Shift-middle mouse button, when the command is active.

functions.name: schSetEnv
functions.description: Sets the value of a schematic environment variable.

functions.name: schSetIgnorePropEnabled
functions.description: Enables or disables a particular ignore property. When you enable an ignore property, this property is applied on an instance while ignoring that instance.

functions.name: schSetOrigin
functions.description: Repositions all the objects in the specified symbol or schematic cellview relative to the new point.

functions.name: schSetPropertyDisplay
functions.signature: schSetPropertyDisplay(?object d_object[?name S_name]?visibility S_visibility)=> l_textDisplays / nil
functions.description: Shows or hides textDisplays containing the name and value of the attribute, property, or parameter of an object. TextDisplay locations are chosen automatically to avoid overlaps with other textDisplays. For more information, see schGetPropertyDisplay and dbCreateTextDisplay.

functions.name: schSetSelectOptions
functions.description: Sets the filter for the selection function. You can select object types by turning toggle switches on or off. You can also choose partial or full selection. Usable when editing schematics or symbols.

functions.name: schSetShapeStyle
functions.signature: schSetShapeStyle(d_shape[ ?color t_colorName ][ ?lineStyle t_lineStyleName ][ ?stipple t_stippleName ][ ?fillStyle t_fillStyleName ][ ?fillColor t_colorName ])=> t / nil
functions.description: Specifies the style attributes of a shape to override the defaults provided by the Display Resource file. Each attribute value must be valid for the current display name.

functions.name: schSetSignalTypeIntegrity
functions.description: Sets the conflict severity for a signal type integrity check (available as part of Schematic Rule Checks) for connections between nets of a specified signal type, and instance pins of specified signal type and direction.

functions.name: schSetSplitPrimaryInst
functions.description: Associates the given split instance with the given split-primary.

functions.name: schSetSplitSymbol
functions.description: Sets up special properties on the cellview to make it a split symbol of g_isSplitSymbol is t. However, if g_isSplitSymbol is nil, the specified cellview is converted to a normal symbol by stripping off the aforementioned properties.

functions.name: schSetSymbolOrigin
functions.description: Moves all the objects in the specified symbol cellview relative to the given origin point.

functions.name: schSetTextDisplayBBox

functions.name: setguard
functions.description: Mainly enforces disciplined use of a symbol as a global variable by associating it with a guarding function that is either a symbol that identifies the name of the guarding function or a lambda form (just like the first argument to the apply function). If the guarding function is nil, the symbol is unguarded. The guarding function is called with two arguments whenever a new value is assigned to the symbol: the symbol and the value to be assigned to it. The result of the guarding function determines the setguard return value that gets assigned to the symbol.

functions.name: setof
functions.description: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setofs
functions.description: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart setof. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setplist

functions.name: setq
functions.description: Sets a variable to a new value. setq is the same as the assignment (=) operator. This is a syntax form.

functions.name: setqbitfield
functions.description: Sets a value into a set of bits in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <:>= operator.

functions.name: setqbitfield1
functions.description: Sets a value into a single bit in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <>= operator.

functions.name: settlingTime
functions.description: The settling time is the time by which the signal settles within the specified Percent of step (theta) of the difference between the Final Value and Initial Value from the Final Value.
